en: Men have generated Agni, the one worthy of praise, from the two fire-sticks by means of their thoughts and the movement of their hands; him who is visible from afar, the lord of the house, the active one.
The Vasus established that Agni in his dwelling, so that he might be well-beheld for protection from every side.
He who is worthy of honor, who has been ever-present in the home—
O Agni, youngest one, kindled, shine forth before us with your unaging flame;
unto you all sacrificial strengths constantly approach.
May these fires, resplendent and rich in heroes, shine forth for you more excellently than other fires,
where well-born men sit together in assembly.
O powerful Agni, by means of our prayer, grant us wealth consisting of brave sons, noble progeny, and high renown.
Him whom no sorcerer, however powerful, can overcome;
to him, the very skillful one, the youthful woman approaches with an oblation of ghee at evening and at dawn;
to him, the seeker of wealth, his own devotion approaches.
O Agni, burn away all hostile powers with those heats wherewith thou didst consume Jarūtha;
drive far away disease and discord. O Vasiṣṭha, pure and radiant purifier, Agni, they kindle thy face.
And through these praises, may you be present here for us.
O Agni, those mortal men of the fathers who have in many places partaken of your countenance—
through them as well, may you be well-disposed toward us here.
May these men, heroes in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless illusions—
those who have praised my exalted prayer.
O Agni, let us not sit in the void among men, nor in the lack of food, nor in the state of being without sons, surrounding you.
May he, the dweller in the dwellings, come to our houses rich in offspring;
may he, accompanied by his steeds, ever approach our sacrifice— our home abounding in progeny and noble descendants,
increasing through his own birth and his abundance.
Protect us, O Agni, from the loathsome Rakṣas; protect us from the malice of the stingy, the evil-minded one.
With you as our ally, may we overcome those who attack us in battle.
This is that Agni who surpasses all other fires, where there is a vigorous son with strong hands.
The syllable with its thousand paths comes together;
that is Agni, who protects from the one who seeks to harm him, and may he deliver his kindler from distress.
Well-born heroes move about him.
This is that Agni, invoked in many places, whom the lord, possessing oblations, kindles with fuel; him the Hotṛ-priest goes around at the sacrifices.
O Agni, may we, being masters, offer to you the many constant oblations.
Both [gods] making the two conveyances for the sacrificial meal— O Agni, carry these most welcome oblations to the assembly of the gods;
let them partake of these fragrant offerings.
O Agni, do not deliver us over to one who has no heroes, nor to ill-will, nor to this lack of devotion;
O observer of Truth, do not give us up to hunger, nor to the demon, neither in our home nor in the forest. Now, O Agni, give guidance to my prayers; you, O God, make them effective for the patrons.
May we both be with you in your bounty; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Agni, you who are easy to invoke and of lovely aspect, shine forth with your brilliant light, O Son of Strength!
Let no harm come to the son born of your own body, nor let a heroic man among us ever fail.
O Agni, do not proclaim us to these poorly maintained fires kindled by the gods for our misfortune. May your ill-willful thoughts, O Son of Strength, the god, never overtake us through haste.
That mortal, O Agni of radiant countenance, who offers oblations to you, the immortal, shall become wealthy.
The god bestows wealth upon him whom the patron, seeking and inquiring, approaches. O Agni, knowing of great prosperity, bring vast riches to our patrons,
by which we, O powerful one, may rejoice with undiminished life and heroic sons.
Now, O Agni, [accept] my prayers...
O Agni, enjoy our fuel today; shine brightly, raising up your worshipful smoke. Touch the celestial ridge with your flames; extend yourself with the rays of the sun.
With sacrifices, let us praise the greatness of these [gods], of Narāśaṃsa, the worshipful one.
They who are wise, pure, and bestowers of inspired thought—the gods who relish both kinds of oblations.
I invoke for you the adorable Asura, the very skillful one, the messenger between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth), whose word is true.

Like Manu, let us magnify Agni, who was kindled by Manu, for the sacrifice that endures forever. Worshiping and bringing [offerings], they spread the sacrificial grass knee-deep with reverence before Agni.
O Adhvaryus, pouring [libations] upon him whose back is sprinkled with ghee, cleanse him with the radiant oblation.

The pious ones, seeking the gods, have thrown open the doors at the divine assembly, eager for the chariot. Like two mothers licking their young, like two noble women anointing themselves at the gathering,
so too are the two celestial maidens, Dawn and Night, who are like a cow that yields milk well for us.
May the two who sit upon the sacred grass, the much-invoked, the bountiful, the worthy of sacrifice, take their place for our well-being.
O sages, poets among men at the sacrifices, I honor you both as Jātavedas, that you may offer worship.
May you elevate our rite during our invocations; may you win desirable boons from among the gods.
RV_07.002.08.1: Let Bhāratī come with the Bhāratīs... RV_07.002.09.1: May that fourth part of ours...
RV_07.002.10.1: O Lord of the Forest, protect us...
Come hither, O Agni... [RV 7.1.11] Make Agni your god, in harmony with the fires, the most excellent sacrificer, the messenger at the sacrifice—
him who is firmly established among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, whose head is flame, whose food is ghee, the purifier.
He snorts like a horse eager for pasture when he has stepped forth from the great enclosure;
then the wind blows after his flame, and your path becomes black. O Agni, when your ageless, kindled flames rise up from you, the newly born bull.
The ruddy smoke goes toward the sky; for as messenger, O Agni, you travel to the gods.
Your splendor has spread across the earth when you have greedily seized the foods with your jaws.
Like an unleashed army, your net advances; O Wondrous One, you consume [the wood] with your tongue as if it were barley.
Men groom him at evening and at dawn—him, the youngest Agni—like a swift steed. Sharpening him as a guest in his own dwelling, the flame of the bull, when offered oblations, has shone forth.
O you of beautiful aspect and lovely countenance, your face shines like gold when you gleam nearby.
Like the thunder of heaven, thy roar goes forth; like the wondrous sun, thou displayest thy radiance.

So that we may worship thee, O Agni, with *svāhā*, with offerings of parched grain and oblations rich in clarified butter— with those immeasurable glories of thine, O Agni, protect us with a hundred fortresses of iron.
Or those unassailable songs which you have for the donor, or those by which you protect the manly ones— O Son of Strength, O Jātavedas, with those guard us, along with our patrons and singers.
Emerging like a polished axe, pure, shining with his own form and body, he has come forth.

RV 7.3.9: He who was born from the two parents, desirable for the sacrifice to the gods, the wise and purifying one— RV 7.3.10: O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a well-disposed will.
May all things be favorable to those who praise and sing your hymns. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Bring forth the oblation and the well-purified hymn for your bright radiance, for Agni,
who moves by his knowledge between all divine and human generations. May that Agni be skillful, even though he is young, from whom, as the youngest, he was born of his mother.

He who embraces the forests, the brightly shining one, immediately consumes even abundant food. In the assembly and presence of this god, whom mortals have seized— the bright one— Agni, who has rejected the human snare, has shone forth for the Āyu, difficult to approach.

This seer among those who are not seers, the wise and immortal Agni, has been established among mortals. O powerful one, do not lead us astray in this matter; may we always be well-disposed toward you.
He who has occupied the seat prepared by the gods—Agni, indeed, has surpassed the immortals through his wisdom.
The plants and the trees bear him as their embryo, and the earth bears him who is the sustainer of all.
For Agni is the lord of abundant immortality; he is the lord of wealth and the giver of heroic strength.
O powerful one, may we not sit around you without sons, without cattle, or without food.
For the wealth of the stranger is to be shared; may we be masters of our own enduring riches.

O Agni, there is no offspring of another that remains as a remnant for one who lacks wisdom; do not lead us astray from our paths. For the stranger, however well-disposed, cannot be grasped by the mind as one’s own kin born of the same womb.
RV_07.004.08.2: Then indeed he comes back again to his dwelling; may the prize-winning steed come toward us, seeking our protection anew.
RV_07.004.09.1: O Agni, you [ward off] those who attack us...
RV_07.004.10.1: These blessings, O Agni, [bestow] upon us...
Bring forth a song of praise to the mighty Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth, who as Vaiśvānara has grown strong in the lap of all the immortals through those who keep watch.
Agni, sought after, has been established in heaven and on earth; he is the leader of the rivers, the bull of the standing waters.
He, Vaiśvānara, shining forth toward the human tribes, grows great through his choice boon.
Out of fear of you, the dark tribes fled, abandoning their food and retreating together.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, as you blazed for Pūru, you shone brightly while shattering their fortresses.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, the earth and the sky, the threefold realm, follow thy law.
Blazing with undying luster, thou hast overspread the two worlds with thy light.
O Agni, the bay horses, the resonant songs, and the ghee-dripping ladles yearn for thee.
The lord of the people, the charioteer of riches, Vaiśvānara, the banner of the dawns and of days—

In you the Vasus have established their divine power (*asurya*), for they take delight in your will, O you who are great like Mitra. O Agni, you drove the Dasyus from their dwelling, generating broad light for the Ārya.
Being born in the highest heaven, like Vāyu, you instantly protect the path.
O Jātavedas, bringing forth the worlds, you cried out toward them, bestowing gifts for the sake of progeny.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, O Jātavedas, impel toward us that glorious nourishment.

O possessor of all boons, with that [power] by which you cause wealth to swell and wide renown for the mortal who offers oblations— O Agni Vaiśvānara, being in harmony with the Rudras and the Vasus, bestow upon us, the liberal patrons, that wealth consisting of abundant food, strength, and fame worthy of renown; grant us great protection.
I proclaim the praise of the sovereign Asura, the man to be celebrated by all peoples; like that of Indra, I laud the deeds of the mighty one, and praising him, I speak of the wood-cutter.
They send forth the sage, the banner, the sustainer, the light from the mountain; he promotes the auspicious sovereignty over heaven and earth.

With songs I celebrate the ancient, mighty deeds of Agni, the shatterer of forts. Agni has driven away those Dasyus—the crafty, the harsh-tongued Paṇis, the faithless, the non-prosperers, and the non-sacrificers; he, the foremost, has made them the last, the ones who do not sacrifice.
He, the most heroic one, who by his powers turned the Dawns—rejoicing in the western darkness—toward the east;
that Agni, the lord of wealth, I praise, the unbending one who subdues those who attack us.
He who made the fortresses tremble with his deadly weapons, and who made the Dawns have a noble husband.
Having subdued Nahuṣa, Agni, the sacrificer, by his mights made the people bringers of tribute. In whose protection all people have taken their stand, seeking to obtain his favor—
Agni Vaiśvānara has sat down in the lap of the two worlds, the parents, as their choice.
The god Vaiśvānara has taken up the treasures of the deep at the rising of the sun;
Agni has taken them from the lower ocean and from the higher, from heaven and from earth.
I impel with salutations the god Agni, the victorious one, like a prize-winning steed.

Be our messenger, you who know the sacrifice; by yourself, you have found your place among the gods, O you of measured pace. Come, O Agni, along your own paths, joyous and taking pleasure in the friendship of the gods.
Making the ridges of the earth roar with your strength, burn down all the forests with your jaws.
The sacrifice is turned eastward, for the sacred grass is well-placed; Agni, being praised, is pleased like a Hotṛ priest.
Calling upon the two Mothers who possess all boons, from whom, O youngest one, you were born most gracious.
At once at the sacrifice, the wise men brought forth the charioteer who belongs to them.
The Lord of the People has been established in the dwelling, Agni, the delightful one, sweet of speech, the observer of Truth.
Having been chosen and having arrived, he has sat down as the bearer of oblations; Agni is the priest in the assembly of men, the distributor of wealth.
He whom both Heaven and Earth have magnified—he, the Hotṛ, who sacrifices for all desirable things.
These men have surpassed all things in splendor—those heroes who have fashioned the choice prayer. They who, listening, have furthered the people, and who have meditated upon this my *ṛta*.
Now we, the Vasiṣṭhas, seek you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength.

RV 7.7.7.2: He has brought nourishment to the singers and the patrons. Do you [gods] protect us always with your blessings! RV 7.8.1.1: The King, the one who triumphs in battle, is kindled with prostrations—he whose face is anointed with clarified butter.
RV 7.8.1.2: Men, pressing forward with oblations, praise him; Agni has shone forth at the head of the dawns.
This Agni here is the great one whose altar is well-known, the delightful invoker for the sacrifice of men.
Having been released upon the earth, he has shone forth; with black-tired wheels, he has grown strong among the plants.
O Agni, by what hymn of praise will you brighten our way? What power will you manifest when you are being lauded?
O Bounteous Giver, when shall we become masters of wealth, winners of riches that are invincible and excellent?
This Agni of Bharata is renowned far and wide, for his great light shines forth like the sun.
He who has stood firm against the Pūrus in battles, the radiant divine guest, has blazed aloft.

In thee, indeed, are many oblations; thou hast become gracious with all thy faces. O Agni, though already praised and lauded, thou art heard; O well-born one, increase thy body of thy own accord. May this word, winning hundreds and thousands, arise for Agni, he who possesses double strength.
May that which brings welfare to the singers and to our kin be glorious, driving away disease and slaying the Rākṣasas.
Now we implore you, O Agni...
The lover of the Dawns has awakened from their lap—the joyous Hotṛ, the most wise sage, the purifier.
He establishes the signal for both kinds of beings; he places oblations among the gods and wealth among the doers of good deeds.
He is the one of skillful wisdom who opens the doors of the Paṇis, purifying for us the hymn that provides much nourishment.
The joyous Hotṛ-priest, the domestic friend of the people, has become visible through the darkness of the nights.
Unerring sage, Aditi, Vivasvat, Mitra—may he be our auspicious guest, speaking kindly to us.
With brilliant radiance, he shines at the forefront of the dawns; the germ of the waters has entered the plants.
He who is to be magnified by you through the ages of man, Jātavedas, has shone forth as he goes to the gathering place.
He who shines forth with a beautiful luster—the cattle have awakened as he is kindled.
O Agni, go on your mission as messenger; do not fail, but proceed toward the gods with the company of those who offer sacred prayers.
Sacrifice to Sarasvatī, to the Maruts, to the Aśvins, and to the Waters; bring all the gods for the bestowal of treasures.
O Agni, Vasiṣṭha, kindling you, has slain Jarūtha; sacrifice for wealth and for abundance.
O Jātavedas, sing your many songs of praise; and may you all protect us evermore.
Like the lover of the Dawn, he has spread his broad radiance, flashing and shining with brilliant luster.
The tawny bull, pure-rayed, shines with his light; impelling our prayers, he has awakened those who desire him.
Like the sun at the dawning of the mornings, he has shone while the eager ones extend the sacrifice like a thought.
Agni, the god who knows all births, hastens as the messenger who goes to the gods, the most effective winner of wealth.

Toward Agni proceed our songs and thoughts, seeking the gods and soliciting wealth—toward him who is beautiful to behold, of fair countenance, swift-moving, the immortal bearer of oblations for human beings.
O Agni, being in harmony with the Vasus, bring Indra to us; and with the Rudras, bring the great Rudra.
With the Ādityas, [they praise] Aditi, the mother of all people; with hymns, Bṛhaspati, who possesses all boons.
The eager clans invoke at the sacrifices Agni, the most youthful, the delightful invoker, the beloved one.
For he has become the protector of riches; unwearied, he is the messenger for the worship of the gods.
The great omen of the sacrifice is not without thee; O Immortal One, they do not rejoice apart from thee.
Come hither on one chariot with all the gods; O Agni, sit down here as the first Hotṛ.
Men, bringing oblations, ever praise thee, the swift one, for the office of messenger.

O Agni, he upon whose sacred grass the gods sit down—for him the days become auspicious. Even the treasures hidden within the threefold darkness have been made manifest for the mortal who offers oblations.
Like Manu, O Agni, worship the gods here; be our messenger and protector against imprecations.
Agni rules over the great sacrifice; Agni [rules] over every oblation that has been prepared.
For the Vasus delight in his ritual wisdom, and thus the gods have established him as the carrier of the oblation.
O Agni, bring the gods here to eat the oblation; let them, with Indra as their chief, rejoice here.

Place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven; do you all protect us evermore with blessings. We have approached with great reverence the youngest [Agni], who has shone forth, well-kindled in his own dwelling—him of wondrous luster, between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing every direction.
Overpowering all difficulties by his greatness, Agni Jātavedas is praised in the home;
may he protect us from misfortune and reproach, both us who sing his praises and our patrons.
O Agni, you are Varuṇa and Mitra; the Vasiṣṭhas exalt you with their prayers.
In you let there be treasures easy to win; do you protect us always with blessings.

Bring forth a prayer and a hymn for Agni, the all-purifying, the illuminator of devotion, the slayer of the Asuras—offer it like an oblation upon the sacred grass to Vaiśvānara, the ordainer of thoughts, as you seek his favor.
O Agni, blazing with your flame, at your birth you filled the two worlds, heaven and earth.
O Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, by your greatness, you released the gods from the curse.
When you were born, O Agni, you looked out upon all beings like a watchful herdsman, a vigilant protector who wanders everywhere.
O Vaiśvānara, find a path for our sacred prayer; do you all protect us evermore.
With fuel and with invocations to the gods, we who are humble shall offer worship to Agni, the god Jātavedas, whose radiance is bright, with oblations.
O Agni, may we worship you with fuel; may we serve you with excellent praise, O Holy One.
May we, O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, serve you with clarified butter; may we, O God of auspicious luster, serve you with the oblation.
O Agni, come to our invocation of the gods together with the deities, graciously accepting our *vaṣaṭ* call.
May we be those who offer gifts to you, the god. Do you all protect us...
Offer the oblation into the mouth of the one who is to be approached, the bountiful giver, who is our closest kin.
He who has sat down as lord over the five tribes in every house— The sage, the master of the home, the youthful one— May he, Agni, protect our household wealth from every side.
And may he protect us from distress. Now I have generated a new hymn for Agni, the falcon of heaven;
will he not surely grant us wealth?
Whose desirable splendors are for all to see, like the wealth of a hero; he blazes at the forefront of the sacrifice.
May Agni accept this *vaṣaṭ*-utterance and graciously enjoy our songs of praise.
The best of sacrificers, the bearer of oblations— O Agni, invoked with offerings, we establish you, the radiant one, rich in heroes, O Lord of the People, as you approach us.
Shine forth through the nights and the dawns; with you as our Agni, may we be well-provided.
You, rich in heroes, are well-disposed toward us.
To you, for the sake of gain, the inspired men come with their prayers.
Possessing a thousand near-syllables,
Agni, the immortal one with bright radiance, drives away the demons;
he is pure, purifying, and worthy of praise.
May he, the lord of power, O young son of strength, bring wealth to us;
may Bhaga also grant what is desirable.
O Agni, you are the glory consisting of heroic sons, as are the god Savitṛ and Bhaga.
And Diti bestows what is desirable.
O Agni, protect us from distress; O God, burn against those who seek to harm us with your most scorching flames, for you are ageless.
Then may the great, unassailable iron fortress of yours protect us for our safety, providing a hundredfold defense.
O dispeller of darkness, guard us from distress and from the one who seeks to strike us down.
Day and night, O invincible one!
With this homage, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength— the beloved, most perceptive messenger, the minister of the well-performed sacrifice, the immortal envoy of all.
He yokes his two ruddy steeds that provide all nourishment; well-invoked, he hastens forward.

The sacrifice is accompanied by excellent prayers and well-performed rites, bringing divine bounty from the Vasus for the people. The flame of this bountiful one has risen as he is being invoked with offerings.
The men kindle Agni, whose smoke rises upward, ruddy and touching the heavens.
We make you our most glorious messenger; bring the gods here for the feast.
O Son of Strength, bestow upon us all the enjoyments of mortals, granting that which we implore of you.
O Agni, you are the master of the house; you are our Hotṛ at the sacrifice. You are the Potṛ, O possessor of all boons, the wise one; perform the worship and bring us what is desirable.
Bestow wealth upon the sacrificer, O you of noble power, for you are indeed the bestower of treasures.
Bring hither the one who is without offense; sharpen every officiant, he whose praise is good and who is skillful.
In thee, O Agni, well-invoked, let the wise patrons be dear—those generous lords of men who control the herds and distribute wide pastures of cattle.

Those for whom the sacrificial offering, with butter in hand, sits down at the door of the house, filling it—protect them from malice and reproach, O Victorious One; grant us shelter that is far-renowned.
He, the bearer of oblations, with his joyous tongue and mouth, is the most wise.
O Agni, bring wealth to our patrons and prepare the offering of the oblation.
Those who bestow gifts of horses and bounties out of a desire for great renown— carry them across distress with your protections, O youngest one, by means of a hundred fortresses.
The god Draviṇodas desires from you a full ladle poured out.
Pour it up, or fill it; then the god will take notice of you.
The gods have made him the wise Hotṛ of the sacrifice, the bearer of the oblation.
Agni bestows treasure and great heroic strength upon the person who worships him and offers oblations.
O Agni, be well-kindled with excellent fuel; let the sacrificial grass be spread out widely.
Let the longing doors be thrown open, and bring hither the yearning gods.
O Agni, partake of the oblation; bring the gods hither; make the sacrifice successful, O Jātavedas!
May Jātavedas make the sacrifice successful; may he worship the immortal gods and satisfy them.
Win for us all desirable things, O wise one; let our prayers be fulfilled this day.
The gods, O Agni, have established you as the bearer of oblations, the son of strength.
May we be those who offer gifts to you, the god; bestowing great treasures upon us, come hither.
For in you alone, O Indra, even our ancestors, the singers, have obtained all desirable things.
In you are the cows that yield milk well, in you indeed are the horses; you are the one most established in wealth for the one who seeks the gods.
For like a king among his subjects, you dwell as a protector through the days, being a wise seer toward those who know. O Maghavan, sharpen our songs with cattle and horses; impel us toward riches.
Here these delightful songs, contending for your favor and longing for the gods, have approached you.
May your path of wealth lead hitherward; may we abide in your goodwill and protection, O Indra.
Like one desiring to milk a cow in a rich pasture, Vasiṣṭha has poured forth his prayers to you.
Everyone calls you my protector; may Indra come toward our benevolence.
Even the spreading floods, O Indra, he made shallow and easy to cross for Sudās. Śimyu, who was growing arrogant, [Indra], the new singer of hymns, turned his curse into a weapon against the rivers.
Puroḷā, Turvaśa, and Yakṣu were eager for wealth, as were the Matsyas, who were like sharpened arrows.
The Bhṛgus and the Druhyus showed obedience; the friend rescued his friend from the two opposing sides.
The Pakthas, Bhalānasas, Alinas, Viṣāṇins, and Śivas all cried out.

He who brought [the cattle] to the assembly of the Ārya, he has come through battle for the Tṛtsus, seeking cattle for the men. Those of evil intent, causing Aditi to flow away, the mindless ones seized the Paruṣṇī. Ruling over the earth, he encompassed it with his greatness; as a seer, he lay watching over the cattle.
They went for the sake of gain, not for loss; even the swift one reached the Paruṣṇī river.
Indra subdued the well-armed enemies of Sudās, those of servile speech among men.
They went like cattle from the pasture without a herdsman, gathering toward their friend as they pleased.
RV 7.18.10: The spotted cattle, sent forth by the spotted one, gave ear; the teams and the chariots were pleased.

RV 7.18.11: He who, out of desire for glory, subdued the twenty-one people of the two Vaikarṇas, the King—like a wondrous craftsman, he trimmed the sacrificial grass in the dwelling; the Hero Indra made their release.
Then the thunderbolt-armed Indra cast down the famous Kavaṣa, who had grown old among the waters, and he struck down Druhyu.
Here, those who sought your friendship and rejoiced after you chose you as their companion for friendship.
Instantly, with his might, Indra shattered all seven of their fortified cities.
For the sake of the Tṛtsus, we have won back the wealth of Vyāna; may we conquer the Pūru who speaks malice in the assembly.
Desiring cattle, the Anavas and Druhyus—sixty hundred and six thousand of them—have fallen asleep.
Sixty heroes and six more have been subdued; all these heroic deeds were performed by Indra.
Impelled by Indra, these Tr̥tsus, performing their service, flowed downward like released waters.
The ill-disposed ones, measuring out their craftiness, abandoned all their provisions to Sudās.
Half of the hero’s [booty] was for the drinker of the cooked oblation; Indra drove the arrogant one far away to the earth.
Indra measured out fury against fury; seeking his own domain, he took to the paths of the way.
Even with the weak he performed that singular deed; even the lioness he struck down with a ram. Indra cut away the corners of the dwelling; he bestowed all provisions upon Sudās.
For all your enemies have always submitted to you; find the weak point even of the defiant Bheda.
O Indra, hurl your sharp thunderbolt at that mortal who acts against him who praises you with this [song].
The Yamunā and the Tṛtsus aided Indra; then he seized Bheda for total destruction.
The Ajas, the Śigrus, and the Yakṣas brought as tribute the heads of horses.
O Indra, your favors and your riches cannot be fully perceived, whether they be ancient or recent, like the dawns.
You slew even Devaka, who thought himself great, and by your own self you struck down Śambara from his lofty height.
Those who, out of devotion to you, have rejoiced in their homes—Parāśara, Śatayātu, and Vasiṣṭha—let them not forget your friendship, O Bhoja; may fair days dawn for these patrons.
Two hundred cattle from Devavān’s grandson, and two chariots with brides from Sudās.
O Agni, worthy one, I go around the gift of Paijavana like a Hotṛ priest at the sacrificial seat, chanting my praise.
The four gifts of Paijavana, adorned with pearls and accompanied by well-disposed horses, stand out in their excellence.
The bay steeds of Sudās, established upon the earth, carry me and my offspring for the sake of progeny and glory.
He whose fame lies between the two wide worlds, who has distributed [wealth] head by head as a distributor;
the seven rivers praise Indra, for he sharpened his weapons for the battle in close combat.
O heroes, Maruts, follow this Sudās, even as you followed Divodāsa, our father.
Favor the intention of Paijavana; [grant him] dominion that is difficult to overcome, undecaying, and worthy of worship.
He who, like a terrible bull with sharpened horns, alone causes all the peoples to tremble;
he who is the bestower of wealth upon every non-giver, providing a treasure for the one who presses the soma.
O Indra, you indeed protected Kutsa in that battle, listening with your own person;
for you, bestowing aid upon the son of Arjuni, subjected the Dāsa Śuṣṇa and Kuyava to him.
O bold one, with all your protections, you boldly helped Sudās, whose oblations were accepted.
You protected Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and you protected Pūru in the winning of land and in the slaying of Vṛtra.
O you whose mind is manly, O Lord of the bay horses, with your heroes you slay many Vṛtras at the banquet of the gods.
You sent the Dasyus Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep, making them easy to kill for Dabhīti.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, those were your mighty exploits when you instantly [overthrew] ninety-nine forts; you cast the hundredth into its dwelling-place, and you slew Vṛtra and Namuci.
These, O Indra, are your ancient provisions for the liberal Sudās, who offers oblations.
For you, the bull, I yoke the two bay stallions; may our prayers reach you, O most powerful one, for the sake of booty.
O Lord of Might, Lord of Bay Steeds, let us not fall into misfortune in this your encounter; protect us with your safe defenses. May we remain dear to you among the patrons.
O Maghavan, may we men, as your dear friends, rejoice under your protection in your favor. Subdue Turvaśa and Yadu, intending to perform a deed worthy of praise for Atithigva.
Even now, O Maghavan, in your favor, the men who recite hymns proclaim their songs of praise.
RV 7.19.9: Those who, with their invocations, have failed to honor you among the Paṇis—choose us for that very alliance.
RV 7.19.10: These hymns of men, O most heroic one, are directed toward you as they offer gifts.
O Indra, be auspicious to them in the slaying of Vṛtra; be the friend, the hero, and the protector of these men.
Now, O heroic Indra, being praised for your aid, strengthened by our prayer, grow great in body. Measure out for us strengths and followers; do you protect us evermore with blessings.
The fierce one, self-dependent, was born for valor—the manly one who, when about to act, makes the waters flow.
The youthful Indra has come to the assembly of men with his aids; he is our protector even from great sin.
Let Indra, waxing mighty, slay Vṛtra; let the hero now protect the singer with his help.
He is indeed the maker of space for Sudās, and he has repeatedly become the giver of wealth to the donor.

The warrior, irresistible, stirrer of battle, the equalizer, the hero, the ever-conquering, unconquered from birth—Indra, by his own power, has scattered the armies; thus he has struck down every foe who acts with enmity. O Indra, mighty one, you have filled both worlds with your greatness and your powers.
Indra, the lord of the bay horses, brandishing his thunderbolt, has spoken aloud in the exhilaration of the soma-draughts.
The Bull begat the Bull for the sake of battle; even a woman has brought forth that hero.
He who stands as the leader of armies for men, the unassailable warrior, the seeker of cattle—he is indeed the bold one.
Never indeed does that man falter, nor does he suffer harm, who seeks to win over his formidable mind.
He who offers worship with sacrifices and pays homage to Indra becomes the master of wealth—he who guards the cosmic order and is born of the cosmic order.
O Indra, when the elder bestows a gift upon the younger, or the superior upon the inferior, it is a favor granted.
Like one seeking immortality, may he sit around [the fire]; O Wondrous One, bring us wondrous wealth from afar.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, that person who is dear to you and has offered gifts in the assembly is your friend.
May we be most highly favored by this benevolence of yours, under the protection and in the hero-guarding care of the Unslayable One.
This hymn has cried out to you like a bull; it has reached you, O Maghavan.
The desire for wealth has come upon your singer; therefore, O Śakra, you are indeed our provider of riches.
O Indra, establish us in that nourishment which comes from you, as well as those wealthy patrons who themselves urge us forward.
RV_07.020.10.2: May there be excellent power for your singer; do you protect us always with blessings. RV_07.021.01.1:
The divine juice, mixed with milk, has been pressed; Indra has taken pleasure in it from his very birth. RV_07.021.01.2:
We awaken you, O Lord of the bay horses, with sacrifices; awaken our hymn of praise in the exhilaration of the soma-juice.
They go forward to the sacrifice; they spread the sacrificial grass; drinking Soma at the assembly, they raise their defiant voices.
The glorious ones are brought down from the grasp [of the enemy]; the roar of the bull-like men resounds afar.
O Indra, you made the many waters flow, which had been obstructed by the serpent, O hero.
At your voice, all artificial things tremble in fear like chariot-steeds; they turn away from you.
Terrible, he has clothed himself in these weapons, knowing all manly deeds.
Indra, exulting, shattered their fortresses; with his thunderbolt in hand, he struck them down by his greatness.
O Indra, most powerful one, neither sorcerers nor those who offer praise have overtaken us with their knowledge.
May he prevail over the hostile folk and the scattered people; let not the phallus-worshippers overcome our truth.
O Indra, through your wisdom you have become great upon the earth; the worlds cannot encompass your majesty.
For with your own inherent power you slew Vṛtra; no enemy has found the end of you in battle. Even the ancient gods measured out their powers for your sake, for your lordly might.
Having overcome all, Indra distributes riches; they invoke Indra for the winning of booty.
For some singer has invoked you for protection, O Indra, lord of abundant prosperity.
You have become our helper, O you of a hundred aids; you are the protector of one such as we who bestows gifts.
O Indra, may we ever be your friends, increasing your glory through our homage, O mighty deliverer.
RV 7.21.9: May they indeed overcome the powers of the attackers with your protection in the encounter; may the hero be unafraid among his enemies.
RV 7.21.10: O Indra, through devotion to you...
RV 7.22.1: Drink the *soma*, O Indra; let that which the stone has pressed for you exhilarate you, O Lord of the Tawny Steeds.
Well-guided by the arms of the presser like a steed,
let that exhilarating draught of yours, which is fit for the yoke and lovely, with which you slay the Vṛtras, O Lord of the Bay Horses—
that let it intoxicate you, O Indra, rich in wealth.

Take heed, O Maghavan, of this speech of mine, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you. Accept these prayers at our joint feast. Hear the call of the one who drinks the pressed juice; take note of the inspired thought of the sage who sings your praise.
Perform the most intimate acts of service; may we be close to you.
I do not forget the hymns of you, the swift one, nor the well-spoken praise of you, the Asura-like lord, for I am wise; ever I proclaim your name, O self-glorious one.
For many indeed are your libations among men; many a time the wise one calls upon you.
O Maghavan, do not keep us away from our enemies for long. All these libations are for you alone, O Hero; for you I fashion these strengthening prayers.
You are to be invoked by men at all times.
O Dasyu-slayer, even now no one can attain the greatness of you who are so esteemed,
nor your heroic power, O Indra, nor your bounty.
RV 7.22.9: Both the ancient seers and those who are new, the inspired poets, O Indra, have generated sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*).
May your auspicious friendships be with us. [And] may you protect us always with blessings. RV 7.23.1:
The sacred prayers have risen up, seeking glory; magnify Indra in the battle, O Vasiṣṭha!
He who by his might has extended across all things—he is the one who listens to the words of one such as I.
A cry has been raised, O Indra, born of the gods, as the tribes strive for mastery in the clash of battle.
For among men, one’s own life-span is not known; therefore, carry us across these calamities.
I harness the booty-seeking chariot with its two bay steeds; my prayers have reached him who delights in them.
Indra, having struck down the resistless Vṛtras, forced asunder these two worlds by his greatness.
Even the waters swelled like barren cows; O Indra, your singers have attained the Truth.
Come hither like Vāyu with his teams; for by our prayers you distribute spoils of war.
May these exhilarating draughts delight you, O Indra, the impetuous one who bestows abundant wealth upon the singer.
For alone among the gods you take pity on mortals; O hero, rejoice at this libation.
Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas honor Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt, with their hymns.
Praised by us, may he protect us with heroic sons and cattle; and do you all protect us evermore.
A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, in this dwelling; come hither to it, O you who are invoked by many men!
So that he may be our protector for our prosperity, may he bestow riches and rejoice in the Soma juices.
O Indra, your mind is seized; the Soma is pressed, the sweet draughts are poured out.
This well-fashioned hymn, with its released flow, brings praise and calls aloud to Indra.
From heaven and from earth, O drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, come to this sacred grass (*barhis*) to drink the Soma.
Let your bay steeds carry you toward me, toward our song of praise, you who are powerful, for the sake of exhilaration.
Come to us with all your aids, being well-pleased, enjoying our prayer, O Lord of the bay horses.
Turning repeatedly with his steadfast [steeds], O fair-cheeked Indra, bestow upon us manly vigor.
This hymn has been offered for the great and fierce one as a vehicle, like a prize-seeking steed. O Indra, this *arkas* praises you; place our glory above the heavens, even as heaven itself.

RV_07.024.06.1 Thus, O Indra, fill us with what is desirable; may we find your great favor. RV_07.024.06.2 Swell the nourishment rich in heroes for our patrons; do you all protect us evermore. RV_07.025.01.1 Your greatness, O Indra...
When the armies, fierce in their common fury, have encountered one another, let the lightning fall from the arm of the hero; let not thy mind wander away in every direction.
O Indra, strike down our enemies in the stronghold—the mortals who assail us.
Drive far away that curse of the reviler; bring us an abundance of riches.
O fair-cheeked one, let a hundred aids be yours for Sudās, and let a thousand praises and gifts attend you.
Strike down the weapon of the mortal who pursues us; bestow upon us glory and treasure.

For I belong to one such as you, O Indra, in wisdom; I belong to one such as you, O Hero, in the gift of protection. Day by day, O fierce one, mighty and dwelling in light, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, act so that we are not disregarded. These Kutsas have brought forth strength for the Lord of the Bay Steeds, seeking in Indra god-sent power.
RV_07.025.05.2: O Hero, make our enemies easy to slay; may we, as conquerors, win the prize. RV_07.025.06.1:
Thus, O Indra, [grant us] a portion of what is desirable... RV_07.026.01.1:
Unpressed Soma has never exhilarated Indra, nor have pressed juices [pleased] Maghavan when offered without prayer.
For him, I generate a hymn that he may enjoy—a new one, like a man—so that he may hear us.

At every hymn, Soma has exhilarated Indra; at every song, the pressed juices have gladdened the Bounteous Lord. When, in their distress, they call upon him for aid with a common resolve, as sons call upon a father.
He has performed these deeds; he will surely perform others now, those which the wise proclaim during the libations.
As a single common husband embraces his wives, so Indra has brought all the fortresses under his control.
Thus they speak of him, and Indra is heard of as the sole distributor of riches, the one who swiftly bestows them.
Whose many aids are swift in rivalry, may his dear and auspicious blessings attend us.
Thus Vasiṣṭha praises Indra, the bull of the peoples, at the soma-pressing for the protection of men.
Bestow upon us thousandfold spoils of war; and do you, O gods, protect us evermore with blessings.
Men invoke Indra in the contest for the prize, when they harness those thoughts that lead to the further shore.
May the Hero, delighting in his strength, grant us a share in the stall rich in cattle in the battle for men.
O Indra, Maghavan, much-invoked one, bestow upon our friends that impetuous power which is yours.
For you, O Maghavan, are firm and wise; open up for us the wealth that is enclosed, as it were.
Indra is the king of the moving world and of the peoples, over all that exists in various forms upon the earth.
From there he bestows riches upon the donor; being praised, he impels the gift hitherward toward us.
Now indeed, may Indra Maghavan, when invoked by us together, bestow strength upon us with his aid—he whose perfect sacrificial fee has overflowed, bringing desirable wealth to the men, our friends.
Now, O Indra, make wide room for us toward riches; may we turn your mind toward us for the sake of bounty.
RV_07.027.05.2: O you who go forth with cattle, horses, and chariots—do you protect us...
RV_07.028.01.1: O Indra, come to our prayer as one who knows; let your bay steeds be harnessed and turned toward us.
RV_07.028.01.2: For all mortals indeed invoke you; hear us, O you who impel all things!
O Indra, your greatness has reached our invocation, for you, O powerful one, protect the sacred prayer (*brahman*) of the seers.
When you, O fierce one, took the thunderbolt into your hand, you became terrible; by your will, you were born invincible.
Under your guidance, O Indra, you brought together the two worlds, like men who call upon you in their distress.
For he was born for great dominion and power; the impeller has indeed sharpened the one who was not yet impelled.
O Indra, be gracious to us through these days, for the peoples with evil friends are being purified.
When Varuṇa, the master of wondrous power, beholds falsehood, he strikes down the sinless man twice over.
We would speak to this Indra, the Maghavan, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty;
he who is most intent upon the prayerful work of the singer. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; come hither, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, to those familiar dwellings.
Drink of this well-pressed, delightful soma, O Maghavan, bestowing gifts as you go.
O Hero, O Brahman, taking pleasure in the performance of the *brahman*, come quickly hither with your bay steeds. Rejoice indeed at this libation; listen closely to these our prayers.
What satisfaction do you find in our hymns? When indeed, O Maghavan, shall we serve you?
I have extended all my thoughts toward you; therefore, O Indra, hear these my invocations.
And truly, there were those human beings for whom you heard the ancient seers.
And so, O Maghavan, I invoke you; you, O Indra, are our providence, like a father.
May we speak forth to Indra...
O God, come to us with power, O impetuous one; be the increaser, O Indra, of this wealth.
O Lord of men, wielder of the good thunderbolt, for great manliness; O hero, for great dominion and heroic power!
They invoke you, the one to be invoked, in the clash of battle, while the heroes strive for their bodies and for the winning of the sun.
You are the one to be honored among all people as the leader of armies; do you, easy to strike, subdue the Vṛtras.
O Indra, may the days dawn as auspicious ones when you set up the foremost banner in battles;
may Agni sit down like a divine Hotṛ-priest, summoning the gods here for the sake of prosperity.
O heroic Indra, we and those who praise you, O God, bestow gifts upon you.
Grant to our patrons the highest protection; may they, being self-sustaining, attain old age.
May we proclaim Indra...
Sing forth a gladdening song for your Indra, the lord of tawny steeds.
O friends, recite the hymn for the Soma-drinker, O bounteous ones, so that we men may offer praise to him who is celestial and whose gifts are true.
O Indra, you desire booty for us; O Śatakratu, you desire cattle;
O Vāsas, you desire gold. O Indra, we who long for you, O Bull, cry out to you aloud.
O Vasu, take note of this of ours; do not deliver us over to the reproach or the censure of the hostile, nor to the one who offers no gifts;
for my mental power is centered in you.
You are a wide-spreading armor and a warrior fighting from the front, O slayer of Vṛtra;
with you as my ally, I speak forth. You are truly great, O Lord of self-sustaining power, whose might follows after you.
Indra and the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) honor you. May that voice, accompanied by the Maruts, encompass you— moving along with us and reaching you together with the days of light.
The drops, rising upward, have found you, the wondrous one, in heaven;
the people bow down together unto you.
Bring forth [the offering] for the great one who increases greatness; offer your devotion to the wise one.
Go forth to the many clans, O filler of the peoples!
For the wide-expanding, mighty Indra, the inspired poets have generated a hymn and a prayer.
The wise do not violate his sacred laws.
The voices have established Indra—the one of unsurpassed fury—as the king for all time, so that he may prevail. Strengthen the allies for the sake of the Lord of the Bay Horses.
Let not even the priests detain you far from us.
Even from afar, come to our communal feast; or being here, listen to us.
For these makers of prayer sit beside your pressed juice like flies on honey.
Desiring wealth, the singers have placed their desire in Indra as one places a foot upon a chariot.
Desiring wealth, I call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt, the one with the excellent right hand, as a son calls upon his father.
These Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra;
O wielder of the thunderbolt, come to our home with your two bay steeds to drink them for exhilaration.

With ears that hear, he comes; may he never neglect our hymns. He who bestows thousands and hundreds at once—no one can restrain him when he wishes to give. That hero, unopposed, has flourished through Indra and through men.
O Vṛtra-slayer, for him who presses out your deep libations and pours them forth, O Maghavan, become the protection of the wealthy patrons when you strike down the defiant.
May we share in the wealth of the one you have struck; bring us a home that is difficult to seize.
Press the Soma for Indra, the drinker of Soma, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
cook the cooked offerings for his aid. Thus, he who bestows gifts brings joy to the giver.
Do not fail, O Soma-pressers! Be skillful for the sake of the Great One; prepare yourselves to strike down poverty.
The one who crosses over conquers, dwells securely, and prospers; the gods do not favor the one who is stingy.
No one has ever obstructed the chariot of Sudās, nor have they brought it to a halt—provided that Indra and the Maruts are his protectors, he shall reach a stall filled with cattle.
May that mortal, seeking booty, win the prize for whom you, O Indra, become a protector. Be the protector of our chariots, O hero, and of our men.
His portion rises up superior, like the wealth of a victor.
RV 7.32.12: Him whom Indra, the lord of the bay horses, protects, no enemies can deceive; he bestows skill upon the Soma-presser.
RV 7.32.13: Offer a hymn that is not deficient, well-placed, and beautifully formed, among those worthy of sacrifice.
Even many snares pass him by who stands firm for Indra through his ritual action.
O Indra, what mortal would dare to challenge you, the possessor of wealth?
O Maghavan, it is through faith alone that the seeker of booty strives to win the prize on the decisive day.
In the battles against Vṛtra, urge on those patrons who bestow beloved treasures.
Under your guidance, O Lord of the Tawny Steeds, may we, together with our patrons, cross over all difficulties.
O Indra, yours is the lowest wealth; you nourish the middle wealth;
you truly rule over all that is highest; no one holds you back from the cattle.
You are renowned as the giver of wealth to all; those who become victorious are yours.
O much-invoked one, this entire earthly world, seeking your aid, begs for your name.
O Indra, if I were the lord of as much wealth as you possess—
O Giver of Wealth, I would cherish the singer; I would not abandon him to misery.
May I bestow gifts day after day upon the one who magnifies me, so that he may find riches wherever they be.
For there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan—not even a father is more dear to us.
The one who crosses over desires to win booty with Purandhi as his ally.
O Indra, much-invoked, I bend you toward me with my song, just as a carpenter bends a well-fashioned felly.
A mortal does not find wealth through ill-praise; nor does riches come to one who falters.
O Maghavan, for one such as I, your gift is truly powerful on the decisive day.
O Hero, we cry out to you like unmilked cows,
to you, Indra, the lord of this moving world who beholds the light of heaven, and the lord of all that stands still.
No other like you, whether celestial or terrestrial, has been born, nor will ever be born.
Desiring horses, O Maghavan Indra, and desiring cattle, we, the seekers of strength, call upon you. Overcome that, O Indra, when the elder [is challenged] by the younger.
O Maghavan, you have indeed been rich in many treasures from of old, and you are to be invoked in every battle.
Drive away our enemies, O Maghavan; make wealth easy for us to find. Be our protector in the great contest for booty; be the strengthener of your friends.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O much-invoked one, on this journey; living, may we attain the light.
Let not unknown, evil-intentioned strongholds, nor those that are unpropitious, step upon us.
With you as our guide, O Hero, may we cross over the flowing waters, the eternal currents.
Turning white, with braided hair on the right, the inspirers of the prayer have indeed gladdened me.
Rising from the sacred grass, I address the men: "The Vasiṣṭhas are not far off for me to protect."
From afar they brought Indra with pressed soma, past the Vaiśanta lake, beyond the fierce one who was drinking.
From the pressed soma of Pāśadyumna Vāyata, Indra chose the Avasiṣṭhas.
Thus indeed he crossed the river with these; thus indeed he slew Bheda with these.
Indra indeed protected Sudās in the battle of the ten kings through your prayer, O Vasiṣṭhas.
O men, through the pleasing prayer of your fathers, you have truly never come to harm, like an unaging axle.
When you Vasiṣṭhas bestowed strength upon Indra with a loud roar during the Śakvarī verses.
Like thirsty men gazing up at the sky, they looked on in distress while hemmed in during the battle of the ten kings.
Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he offered praise; he made wide room for the Tṛtsus.
Like sticks used for driving cattle, the Bharatas were cut down and left as a small remnant.
And Vasiṣṭha became their leader from the beginning; the tribes of the Tṛtsus spread abroad.
Three create seed within the worlds; three noble lineages have light as their foremost part.
Three heats accompany the Dawn; the Vasiṣṭhas know them all.
Their brilliance is like the rising of the sun; their greatness is as profound as the ocean.
Like the speed of the wind, O Vasiṣṭhas, your hymn of praise cannot be followed by any other. They, with the insights of their hearts, move toward the secret that has a thousand branches.
Wearing the garment stretched out by Yama, the Apsarases approached, becoming Vasiṣṭhas.
When Mitra and Varuṇa beheld you emerging from the light of the lightning,
that was one of your births, O Vasiṣṭha, when Agastya brought you forth for the sake of the people.
And you, O Vasiṣṭha, are the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, born from the mind of Urvaśī, O Brahman. All the gods received you as a fallen drop by means of divine prayer within the lotus-leaf.
He is the conscious one, the knower of both worlds, the giver of thousands or indeed the giver of all.
Intending to weave the enclosure stretched out by Yama, Vasiṣṭha was born from the Apsarases.
Born at the sacrificial session, urged on by their homages, the two poured their common seed into a jar.
From its midst, Māna rose up; therefore they call the seer born therefrom Vasiṣṭha.
He bears the bearer of the *uktha* and the bearer of the *sāman*; bearing the pressing-stone, he speaks first.
Approach him with well-disposed minds; Vasiṣṭha, the piercer, shall come to you.
Let the divine *manīṣā* (inspired thought) go forth from us, like a well-fashioned, prize-winning chariot.
They know the origin of earth and heaven; they hear the waters as they flow. Even the broad waters swell for him; among the Vṛtras, the fierce ones consider themselves heroes.
Place the horses at his yoke-poles—Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose arms are golden.
Like one who sets out for a sacrifice, like a traveler on his path, urge yourselves forward by your own power!
By your own power, urge the sacrifice forward in battles; set up the banner, the hero, for the people!
From his vital strength the light has emerged; he bears the burden as the earth bears the world.
RV 7.34.8: O Agni, I invoke the gods who are not sorcerers; accomplishing [my purpose] through Truth, I fashion my prayer.
RV 7.34.9: Direct your divine prayer toward us; send forth your speech to the gods. RV 7.34.10:
Varuṇa, the fierce one with a thousand eyes, beholds from close at hand the course of these rivers.
King of kingdoms, the ornament of rivers—may sovereign power and full vitality belong to him.

Protect us among all the tribes; today, render the praise of the reviler devoid of splendor. May the malevolent bolt of our enemies pass away; drive far from us every affliction that touches our bodies.
May Agni graciously accept our oblations along with our salutations; this most beloved hymn has been offered to him.
In harmony with the gods, make the Son of the Waters your friend; may he be auspicious to us.
With hymns I praise Ahi, the water-born, who sits at the base of the rivers in the mid-regions.
May Ahibudhnya not deliver us over to harm; may the sacrifice of this upholder of *ṛta* not fail.
And may they bestow glory upon these our men; let the bold enemies advance toward wealth.
They scorch the enemy with their heat, like the sun upon the earth, for they possess great armies and impetuous might.
When the wives come toward us, may Tvaṣṭṛ, the fair-handed, bestow heroic sons upon us.
May Tvaṣṭṛ accept our hymn of praise; may Aramati, seeking wealth, be with us.
May they, the givers of gifts, grant us riches; may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, with his protective powers, be our secure refuge; may he, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us.
May the mountains grant us that wealth, and may the waters, the plants that follow the gift, and the sky grant it to us.
May the earth, in harmony with the lords of the forest, and may both heaven and earth protect us on every side.
May the two vast worlds, heaven and earth, yield to that; may the celestial Varuṇa, with Indra as his companion, yield;
and may all the Maruts, who are powerful, yield. May we be the sustainers of wealth, so that our prayer may be fulfilled.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the plants, and the trees take pleasure in this for us.
May we be in the protection, in the lap of the Maruts. Do you protect us always with blessings...
May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their aids; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Soma be for our well-being, for peace and prosperity; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty.
May Bhaga be auspicious for us; may our praise be auspicious; may Purandhi be auspicious for us, and may riches be auspicious.
May the praise of the true and well-governed be auspicious for us; may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious for us.
May Dhātṛ be auspicious for us, and may Dhartṛ be auspicious for us; may the far-reaching [goddess] be auspicious for us with her self-sustaining powers.
May the two vast worlds, Heaven and Earth, be auspicious; may the mountain be auspicious to us; may the propitious invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.
May Agni, whose face is light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us.
May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.
May Heaven and Earth be auspicious for us at our first invocation; may the atmosphere be auspicious for us, visible and gracious.
May the plants and the trees be auspicious for us; may the victorious Lord of the Atmosphere be auspicious for us.
May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious for us; may Varuṇa, the one of fair praise, be auspicious along with the Ādityas.
May Rudra with the Rudras be auspicious to us, the healer; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine dames hear us here for our welfare.
May Soma be auspicious to us, may the sacred prayer be auspicious to us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious to us, and may the sacrifices be for our well-being.
May the fashioning of the sacrificial posts be auspicious to us; may the plants be auspicious to us, and may the altar be for our well-being.
May the far-seeing Sūrya rise for our welfare; may the four quarters of space be auspicious for us.
May the firm mountains be auspicious for us; may the rivers and the waters be for our peace.
May Aditi be auspicious for us through her sacred laws; may the Maruts, the singers of beautiful hymns, be auspicious for us.
May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may the path of existence be auspicious to us, and may Vāyu be auspicious to us.
May the god Savitṛ, our protector, be auspicious to us; may the dawns that shine forth be auspicious to us.
May Parjanya be auspicious to our offspring, and may the Lord of the Field be a source of well-being to us.

May the All-Gods be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our inspired thoughts, be auspicious. May those who accompany us be auspicious, and those who grant gifts be auspicious; may the celestial and terrestrial beings be auspicious to us, and may the waters be auspicious to us.
May the Lords of Truth be auspicious to us; may the swift steeds be auspicious, and may the cattle be auspicious to us.
May the *Ṛbhus*, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious to us; may the Fathers be auspicious to us in our invocations.
May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahibudhnya and the Ocean be auspicious to us.
May Apām Napāt, the protector, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, whose guardian is the gods, be auspicious to us.
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly fashioned prayer being performed.
May the celestial ones and those of the earth hear it, as well as those born of the cow and those who are worthy of sacrifice.
Those among the gods who are most worthy of sacrifice, who are to be honored by Manu, the immortal ones who know the cosmic order (ṛta).
May they grant us wide-striding space today; do you all protect us evermore with blessings! Let this prayer proceed from the seat of Order; Sūrya has released the cows with his rays.
The broad earth has spread out with its ridges; Agni has been kindled upon her wide surface.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, O Asuras, I offer this newest hymn to you both like a refreshing draught. One of you two is a powerful, unerring leader on the path; and Mitra, speaking, stirs the people. The arrivals of the rushing wind have come; they have swelled like milch-cows and like streams of honeyed milk.
Born in the seat of the great heaven, the bull has bellowed in this very udder.
O Indra, hero, may I with my song bring hither those two beloved, well-yoked bay steeds of yours that are ever-ready.
May I turn toward me the wise Aryaman, who frustrates the wrath of the one who seeks to harm.
Worshipful ones, they sacrifice for his friendship and vital strength in their own abode of *ṛta*.
Being praised by men, he has distributed nourishments; this most beloved homage is for Rudra.
When the glorious ones, lowing together, [gather]—Sarasvatī, the seventh, whose mother is the river.
Those who bring forth easily, yielding well, with good streams, swelling with their own milk;
and may those Maruts, rejoicing, protect our prayer and our offspring, O you who possess strength.
May the imperishable moving waters not overlook us; they have increased for us that wealth which is worthy of union.
Bring forward your great Aramati, and Pūṣan, like a hero fit for the assembly;
bring Bhaga, the protector of this our prayer, Vāja who bestows gifts, and Purandhi, for the sake of winning booty.
O Maruts, let this song of praise go forth toward you, and toward Viṣṇu, the protector of the poured libation, with our prayers for aid.
And bestow strength upon the progeny and upon the one who praises you; do you ever protect us with blessings.
O Vājās, O Ṛbhukṣans, let your most swift and unassailable chariot bring you hither to be praised.
At the libations, fill yourselves with the triple-backed Soma-draughts for exhilaration, O you of fair helmets, with your great [powers].
You indeed bestow treasure upon the bounteous patrons, O R̥bhukṣans who behold the light of heaven, an unimpaired gift.

Drink together at the sacrifices, O self-dependent ones; distribute riches to us through our prayers. For you have spoken, O Bounteous One, regarding the granting of gifts in the distribution of great and small wealth.
Both your hands are filled with wealth; your bounty does not withhold riches.
O Indra, you are self-glorious, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, like a successful prize-winner; as a singer, you go to the setting place.
May we, the Vasiṣṭhas, now be your worshippers, performing sacred prayer for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds.
You are the winner of the heights even for the donor, you with the bay horses, through whose prayers you have entered [into us].
We have indeed won through your allied aids; when, O Indra, will you grant us wealth?
You clothe us, as it were, like wise priests; when, O Indra, will you take notice of our speech?
May the swift steed, through our ancestral prayer, bring us wealth with brave sons and nourishing food even unto our home.
Though even the goddess Nirṛti has power over him whom men have made homeless and aged, may the autumns rich in nourishment reach Indra.
May he whose kin are threefold come to one who has reached old age, whom mortals have deprived of his own dwelling.
RV 7.37.8.1: May bounties come to us, O Savitṛ, for our praise; may riches come in the granting of the mountain.
May the divine protector always attend to us. [Do you all protect us ever with blessings. RV 7.37.8.2:
Upward has that god Savitṛ extended this golden intention which he has sent forth on his journey.
Truly, Bhaga is to be invoked by men—he who, possessing abundant wealth, bestows many treasures.
Arise, O Savitar, and hear this, O golden-handed one, at the presentation of the sacred Law (*ṛta*).
Casting away narrow-mindedness, you bestow upon men the wide, broad, and ample food that sustains mortals.
May the god Savitṛ be praised, whom even all the Vasus and the Aśvins extol.
May he, worthy of homage, graciously accept our hymns and protect our patrons with all his guardians.
He whom the goddess Aditi praises, taking pleasure in the impulsion of the god Savitṛ.
Varuṇa, the sovereign, praises [us], as do Mitra and Aryaman in unison;
they who, mutually striving, together bestow the bounty of heaven and earth, the givers of gifts.
May Ahibudhnya also hear us, and may Varūtrī protect us along with the Ekadhenu cows.
May the Lord of the Family, being entreated, grant us that treasure of the god Savitṛ.
The mighty one calls upon Bhaga for protection; even the weak man goes to Bhaga for his treasure.
May the Vājins be auspicious to us in our invocations at the assembly of the gods—those who run their measured course and sing beautiful hymns.
Crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, drive away all diseases far from us.
O swift ones, protect us in every contest for booty; O wise, immortal, knowers of the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), protect us in our strivings for wealth.
Drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; being satisfied, go by the paths traveled by the gods.
Agni, standing upright, has established his favor toward the wealthy; his flame moves forward toward the assembly of gods.
The two pressing-stones have taken their path like chariot-drivers; may the Hotṛ-priest, impelled, sacrifice for us according to the Eternal Law (ṛta).
The sacrificial grass (barhis), easy to tread upon, has been spread out for them; like two lords of the people, they go toward the central ridge.
At the first invocation of the people at the dawning of the light, may Vāyu with his team of horses and Pūṣan come for our well-being.
Here on earth, the Vasu gods have taken their pleasure; the radiant ones have purified themselves in the wide mid-air.
O you of broad strides, turn your paths hitherward; hear this messenger of ours who has come to you.
For they, the worshipful protectors at the sacrifices, all the gods, occupy their common dwelling place.

O Agni, sacrifice at the rite to those who desire it—with prompt obedience—to Bhaga, the Nāsatyas, Purandhi, Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni; bring them hither from heaven and earth by our songs of praise.
May Aryaman, Aditi, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the Maruts take delight in these [oblations].
I have offered the oblation with hymns to those worthy of sacrifice; may he, insatiable, reach the desire of mortals.
May the Ordainer grant wealth that is never-failing and ever-conquering; may we now indeed be united with the gods as our allies.

Now may Heaven and Earth be praised by the Vasiṣṭhas; may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, the upholders of *ṛta*, grant us our most excellent hymn of praise. O radiant ones, protect us evermore with your blessings!
May the hearing that belongs to the assembly come hither; let us offer this hymn of praise to the swift ones.

Whatever Savitṛ, the god, shall impel today, may we be among those who share in his precious wealth. May Mitra, Varuṇa, the two worlds (Heaven and Earth), Indra, and Aryaman grant us that which is allotted by the gods.
May the goddess Aditi assign us riches, as well as Vāyu and Bhaga, who yoke their teams.
O Maruts, let that mortal be fierce and powerful whom you, whose horses are speckled, protect.
And him Agni and Sarasvatī impel; there is no one who can surpass his wealth.
For Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—the kings—along with the Waters, are the leaders of the *ṛta*.
May the goddess Aditi, who is easily invoked and free from enemies, carry us across distress unharmed.
With oblations, we approach at the offering of this bounteous god Viṣṇu, the impetuous one.
For Rudra knows his own Rudra-power; O Aśvins, come on your radiant path.
O Pūṣan, be not hot-tempered or envious; may Varūtrī and the Rātiṣācīs grant us gifts.
May the joy-bestowing coursers protect us; may the wind, wandering all around, bestow rain upon us.
Now, O Heaven and Earth...
At dawn we invoke Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins.
At dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn we shall call upon Soma and Rudra.
We shall invoke the fierce Bhaga, the winner of the morning, the son of Aditi who is the sustainer.
Even the weak man who considers himself strong, even the king—who says, "May I partake of Bhaga as my portion.
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, grant us this prayer and bestow it upon us.
O Bhaga, further us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, further us with men, and may we be rich in heroes.
And may we now be fortunate, both at the onset of the day and at its midpoint;
and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan, may we abide in the favor of the gods.
O Gods, let Bhaga alone be the fortunate one; through him may we be fortunate.
O Bhaga, everyone invokes you; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here.
May the Dawns incline toward our sacrifices, as [they do] toward the pure station of Dadhikrāvan.
May they bring hither to us Bhaga, the finder of wealth, as spirited horses draw a chariot.
May the auspicious Dawns—rich in horses, rich in cattle, and rich in heroes—ever shine upon us.
Yielding clarified butter and overflowing on every side, may you protect us evermore.
The *brahmans* and the *Aṅgirases* have approached; let the roar of the celestial steed be heard.
The milch-cows, swimming in the waters, have lowed; let the two pressing-stones be yoked, the ornament of the sacrifice.

O Agni, well-known from of old is your path; yoke for the pressed juice your bay and ruddy horses, or those red steeds that carry heroes to the seat. Seated here, I invoke the generations of the gods.
I celebrate your sacrifice together with reverent salutations; may the joyous Hotṛ-priest excel in our presence.
O you of many aspects, worship the gods well; may you turn hither the godly *Aramati*.
When the guest of the wealthy hero, resting comfortably in his dwelling, has made himself known.
Agni, well-pleased and well-established in the house, bestows what is desirable upon this people.
O Agni, enjoy this sacrifice of ours; make us glorious among the Maruts and Indra.
Let Night and Dawn sit upon the sacrificial grass; worship here Mitra and Varuṇa, who are eager for the rite.
Thus Vasiṣṭha, desiring wealth of all kinds, has praised the victorious Agni. May he extend for us food, riches, and strength. Do you protect us always with blessings!
At your sacrifices, those seeking the gods sing forth with adorations to Heaven and Earth, so that they may grant us nourishment.

Those whose peerless sacred hymns, like the branches of a tree, spread out in all directions, O sages—let the sacrifice proceed like a swift steed toward its goal; lift up the ladles dripping with ghee with one mind.
Spread the sacrificial grass well for the rite; the upward-pointing flames, seeking the gods, have arisen.
Like sons carried on their mother’s lap, let the gods sit upon the back of the sacred grass (*barhis*).
Let the all-pervading one anoint the sacrificial assembly; O Agni, do not neglect us in the assembly of the gods.
They have served you according to your pleasure, O worshipful ones, milking the well-yielding streams of Truth (*ṛta*).
Come today to the great assembly of you Vasus, the eldest; come together with one mind as you are gathered here.
Thus, O Agni, bestow your favor upon us among the people; through you, O powerful one, may we be unassailable.
May we, rejoicing together with you as our ally, be unharmed through wealth. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings!
I invoke Dadhikrā for you first, the Aśvins, Uṣas, and the kindled Agni, and Bhaga for our protection;
Indra, Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sun.
Awakening Dadhikrā with homage, rising up and proceeding toward the sacrifice.
Seating the goddess Iḷā upon the sacred grass, we, the inspired singers, invoke the Aśvins who are easily summoned.
Awakening Dadhikrāvan, Agni, the Dawn, the Sun, and the Cow,
and the ruddy steed of Varuṇa, the brown one— may they all drive away from us every misfortune.
Dadhikrāvan, the first prize-winning steed, comes to the front of the chariots, knowing the way.
In harmony with the Dawn, with Sūrya, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases—
may Dadhikrā anoint our paths so that we may follow the path of Ṛta.
May the divine host hear us, may Agni hear, and may all the mighty, wise ones hear.
May the god Savitṛ, rich in treasures, come filling the mid-air, borne by his horses; holding many gifts for men in his hand, he settles the world and impels it forth.

Raising his two great, relaxed arms, golden-hued, he has reached to the ends of heaven. Now indeed shall that majesty of his be praised; even the Sun yields to him in his active power. May that god Savitar, the powerful lord of treasures, grant us riches.
Taking his stand, he bestows upon us far-reaching intelligence and the food that mortals enjoy. These songs praise Savitar, the fair-tongued, whose arms are full and whose hands are skillful.
May he grant us wonderful, lofty vital strength. And may you all protect us evermore with blessings!
RV 7.46.1: Bring these songs to Rudra, the god who possesses a firm bow, swift arrows, and self-sustaining power;

to the invincible, the conqueror, the ordainer, whose weapons are sharp—let him hear us. RV 7.46.2: For he, by his dominion over the earthly race and by his sovereignty over the celestial, takes heed.
Open wide for us the doors that grant abundance; O Rudra, be free from malice toward our offspring.
May that bolt of yours which, released from heaven, moves across the earth, pass us by.
O you whose breath is sweet, there are a thousand medicines at your command; do not harm our children or our descendants.
Do not slay us, O Rudra; do not abandon us. May we not fall under the wrathful strike of your anger.
Grant us a share in the sacred grass (*barhis*) and in the praise of the living. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
O Waters, that wave of yours which those seeking the gods first fashioned as the drink of Indra—O *īḷā* (nourishing one)—[that we invoke].
May we today win from you that pure, stainless, honey-sweet wave which sprinkles ghee.
May Apāṃ Napāt, the swift impeller, protect that most honeyed wave of yours, in which Indra rejoices with the Vasus; may we, as seekers of the gods, attain it this day.
Flowing with a hundred purifiers, rejoicing through their own inherent power (*svadhā*), these goddesses go to the path of the gods.
They do not violate the laws of Indra; offer an oblation rich in clarified butter (*ghṛta*) to the rivers.
Those whom Sūrya has extended with his rays, and for whom Indra carved a path and a wave—
O rivers, grant us wide space; do you protect us always with blessings.
O R̥bhukṣans, O Vājas, O heroes, O bounteous ones, rejoice among us in the pressed soma.
May your powers, like those of travelers, turn hitherward; may they bring the broad, manly chariot.
May we overcome you with the *Ṛbhus*, as the *Ṛbhu* is; with the *Vibhus*, as the *Vibhu* is, may we prevail through power over powers.
May Vāja favor us in the winning of booty; with Indra as our ally, may we overcome Vṛtra.
For they indeed surpass many [enemies] by their command; the noble one conquers all through his superior strength.
May Indra, Vibhvan, R̥bhukṣan, and Vāja—the noble ones—destroy the strength of the enemy through their conflict.
O gods, now create wide space for us; may you all, being of one mind, be present for our protection. May the Vasus grant us nourishment. Do you protect us evermore with blessings.
Led by the ocean, purifying themselves from the midst of the flood, they flow on without resting.
May those divine waters, which Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, dug out, protect me here.
Those waters that are celestial, or those that flow [on earth], whether dug out or self-born—may they protect me.
Those waters which have the ocean as their goal, which are pure and purifying— those waters...
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men—
those waters which drip sweetness, which are pure and purifying— those waters...
In whom King Varuṇa, in whom Soma, and in whom all the gods rejoice in strength;
in whom Agni Vaiśvānara has entered—those are the waters...
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect me here; do not let that which destroys the nest and pervades all reach us.
The goat-footed one, difficult to behold, I have hidden away; let not the creeping disease find me with its foot.
Whatever eruption has appeared upon the joints of the body, let it affect the knees and the ankles.
May Agni, glowing with heat, drive that away from here; let not the creeping disease find me...
Whatever poison is in the *śalmali* tree, whatever is in the rivers, and whatever is born from the plants—may all the gods drive that away from here; let it not touch me with its foot.
Those [regions] which are slopes, hollows, and heights, those which are watery and those which are waterless.
May they, swelling with milk for us, be auspicious goddesses free from the *śipada* disease; may all the rivers be free from the *aśimidā* disease.
Through the newest protection of the Ādityas, through their most peaceful shelter, may we prevail.
May the swift ones, listening to us, establish this sacrifice in sinlessness and in the state of Aditi.
May the Ādityas and Aditi rejoice; may Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, who are most upright, be ours. May they, the guardians of the world, drink the Soma for our protection today.
All the Ādityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, and all the Ṛbhus—may they all [rejoice].

Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins have been praised; do you protect us always. May we be free from affliction, O Ādityas, among the gods and among mortals, O Vasus. Winning, may we win, O Mitra and Varuṇa; being, may we be, O Heaven and Earth.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, our guardians, grant us this protection for our children and descendants. May we not suffer for the sin committed by another; O Vasus, may we not do that which you punish.
The swift Aṅgirases, approaching, have attained the treasure of the god Savitṛ.
May our great Father and all the gods, being of one mind, graciously accept this, O worshipful ones.
