With sacrifices and prostrations, I fervently invoke the two vast and worshipful worlds, Heaven and Earth.
For indeed, the ancient seers, singing praises, placed those two great ones, who have the gods as their parents, at the forefront.
With newest songs, bring hither the two first-born parents to the seat of the Eternal Law.
O Heaven and Earth, come to us with the divine host; great is your protective shelter.
For indeed, O Heaven and Earth, you possess many treasures for the liberal giver.
RV 7.53.3.2: Grant us that which may be unfailing and free from distress; do you protect us always with blessings.
RV 7.54.1.1: O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us! Be a gracious refuge for us and free from disease. RV 7.54.1.2:
Whatever we implore of you, accept that favorably; be a source of well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds.
O Vāstoṣpati, be our furtherer; O Indu, increase our household with cattle and horses. May we remain unaging in your friendship; favor us as a father favors his sons.
O Vāstoṣpati, may we be united with your powerful assembly, which is delightful and provides a path to prosperity.
Protect us in peace and in exertion; grant us what is best. And do you all protect us...
O Lord of the Dwelling, dispeller of disease, entering into all forms, be a most gracious friend to us.
O Arjuna, O Sarama’s son, O tawny one, when you bare your teeth and flash like gleaming spears, as you snap at the corners of our mouths, fall fast asleep! O Sarama’s son,
pursue the thief or the robber, and go back again!
RV_07.055.03.2: You make sport of Indra’s praisers; why do you seek to bring misfortune upon us? Go to sleep! RV_07.055.04.1: You tear up the boar; let the boar tear you up! RV_07.055.04.2:
[You make sport of] Indra’s praisers...
May the mother sleep; may the father sleep; may the dog sleep; may the lord of the house sleep. May all kinsmen sleep; may this person around us sleep.
May he who sits, he who walks, and whatever person looks upon us, sleep.
We shall crush their eyes, just as we have this palace.
The bull with a thousand horns who rose up from the ocean— by him, the powerful one, we lull the people to sleep.
The women who sleep on couches, those who sleep on beds, and those who lie upon their mattresses—

those women who possess auspicious fragrances, all of them we cause to sleep. Who are these men, clearly manifest, dwelling in the same nest, the youthful servants of Rudra, accompanied by their own horses?
No one indeed knows their births; they alone truly know each other’s place of origin.
They have sown themselves with their own pure powers; roaring like the wind, these falcons have contended together.
The wise man has discerned these secrets: that the great Pṛśni bore them in her udder.
May that host, accompanied by the Maruts, be rich in heroes—eternally victorious, increasing manly strength.
They are the swiftest on their course, most beautiful in splendor, united with glory, and fierce in their vital powers.
Fierce is your power and firm your strengths; thus, with the Maruts, the host is exceedingly mighty.
Resplendent is your breath, wrathful are your minds; like a roaring sage is the spirit of your bold host. Keep your lightning bolt far away from us; let not your ill-will reach us here.
I invoke the dear names of you, the swift ones, so that the Maruts, being satisfied and longing, may come.
Well-armed, impetuous, adorned with beautiful golden neck-ornaments, they themselves beautify their own bodies.
O Maruts, pure are the oblations for you who are pure; I present this pure sacrifice to the pure ones.
Through the *ṛta* (Cosmic Order) they have come, the upholders of *ṛta*, born of purity, pure, and purifying.
Upon your shoulders, O Maruts, are the rings; upon your chests rest the golden ornaments.
Shining like flashes of lightning with their rains, you advance according to your own nature, brandishing your weapons.
Your greatnesses, rising from the depths, surge forth; O you who are worthy of sacrifice, extend your names far and wide.
O Maruts, enjoy this thousandfold portion of the domestic animal, intended for the household sacrifice. O Maruts, if you take heed of this praise of the inspired singer who offers the oblation,
then quickly grant us wealth with heroic sons— wealth that no stingy man shall ever harm.
The Maruts, who are swift like coursers and self-moving, have adorned themselves like youths visible to the seer;
they stand in their mansions like brilliant children, playing like calves that drink milk.
May the Maruts, bestowing gifts upon us, be gracious, making heaven and earth well-established and wide.
Far be your bolt that slays cattle and slays men; O Vasus, bow down to us with your favors!
The Hotṛ-priest, having sat down and praising you, repeatedly invokes you, O Maruts, for your all-encompassing bounty.
He who has such a protector as you, O Bulls, he, free from duplicity, calls upon you with hymns.
These Maruts bring the swift to rest; these bend force with force. They protect the singer from the one who seeks to harm him, and they lay heavy hatred upon the stingy foe.
These Maruts impel even the sluggish, just as the Vasus take pleasure in the restless one.
O bulls, drive away the darkness; bestow upon us all progeny and offspring.
O Maruts, may we not be excluded from your gifts; let us not be left behind in the distribution of wealth, O chariot-borne ones.

Grant us a share in that desirable wealth which you, O mighty ones, possess as something well-born. When men, being heroes, clash together in their fury over the great waters, the plants, and the settlements— then, O Maruts, sons of Rudra, be our protectors in the battles for our lives.
O Maruts, you have performed many ancestral deeds, those hymns which are recited for you even from of old.
Through the Maruts, the fierce one is victorious in battles; through the Maruts, the steed wins the prize.
O Maruts, may there be among us a vigorous hero, a lord who is the sustainer of men.
RV 7.56.24: By means of which we may cross over the waters for a secure dwelling, may we then abide in our own home under your protection.
RV 7.56.25: May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni grant this to us.
RV 7.57.1: O worshipful Maruts, your name is "the Sweet"; you rejoice with power at the sacrifices.
They who cause even the two vast worlds to tremble, they who, as fierce ones, swell the spring when they have gone forth;
for the Maruts are the perceivers of the one who praises them and the leaders of the sacrificer’s thought.
Today, at our assemblies, sit upon the sacred grass, being well-pleased, for the feast.
No others shine so much as these Maruts do, with their golden ornaments, their weapons, and their bodies.

Adorning both heaven and earth, they, the all-adorned ones, anoint themselves alike for the sake of splendor. May that bolt of yours, O Maruts, be far away when we have committed any offense against you through human frailty.

O worshipful ones, may you not be angry with us even for that [offense]; may your most gracious favor be with us. O Maruts, blameless, pure, and purifying, take delight even in what has been done here.
Protect us with your favors, O worshipful ones; further us with your strengths so that we may prosper.
And may the Maruts, being praised, come to our oblations with all their names, O heroes.
Grant us a portion of immortality for our progeny; awaken for us riches, true boons, and gifts.
O Maruts, being praised, come hither with all your aids toward the patrons for the sake of complete prosperity.
RV_07.057.07.2: Those who by their own selves increase us a hundredfold—do you protect us... RV_07.058.01.1: Sing forth to the troop that sprinkles together, which is mighty in the divine abode.
RV_07.058.01.2: And they shake the two worlds with their greatness; they reach the firmament from the depth of destruction.
Even from their very birth, O Maruts, you are fierce in your splendor, terrible, impetuous, and tireless.
You who prevail through your greatness and your might—at your approach, every beholder of the light trembles with fear.
Bestow great vital strength upon our patrons; may the Maruts graciously accept our fair praise.
The path traveled does not obstruct the person; may you further us with your desirable aids.
O Maruts, the inspired singer favored by you possesses hundreds; the victorious steed favored by you wins thousands.
The sovereign king favored by you slays the enemy; let that gift of yours be manifest, O shakers.
I desire to win over those Maruts, the bounteous sons of Rudra; will they not surely turn toward us again?
Whatever they have been angry with us for in secret or openly, we pray for that forgiveness from those who are swift.
This well-spoken praise of the generous ones has been uttered; may the Maruts take pleasure in this hymn.
O Bulls, drive away hatred even from afar! [And] may you protect us always with blessings!
O Gods, him whom you protect here and there, and him whom you lead—O Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Maruts, grant protection to that man!
O Gods, by your protection on the day of battle, the sacrificer who loves you overcomes his enemies.
He extends his dwelling and increases his great provisions who gives to you according to your desire. Vasiṣṭha does not disregard even the lowliest among you.

O Maruts, all of you who desire it, drink today at our pressed juice. For your aid in battles does not fail the man to whom you have granted your favor, O heroes. Your newest benevolence turns toward us; come quickly, you who long to drink.
O you who are impetuous, come quickly with your gifts to drink these soma-juices!
O Maruts, I have offered these oblations to you; do not go elsewhere.
Sit upon our sacred grass, protect us, and grant us desirable wealth.

O Maruts, never failing in your purpose, rejoice here in the sweet Soma juice; Svāhā! For even those who adorn their own bodies have flown down like swans with dark-blue backs. O heroes, like joyful men, sit down on all sides around me at the libation, exulting in the draught.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whoever, harboring malice, seeks to strike down our thoughts from the side—he, the hater, let him be caught in his own snares; strike him down with your most scorching blow!
O Sāntapana Maruts, enjoy this oblation!
O Maruts, you who destroy enemies by the millions, come to our domestic sacrifice; do not stay away from us,
O bounteous givers, for we seek your aid.
Right here, O Maruts, you who are self-strong, poets with sun-bright skins, I choose your sacrifice. We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity.
Like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be released from death, not from immortality.
O Sūrya, as you rise today, speak the truth for Mitra and Varuṇa that we are sinless. O Aditi, O Aryaman, may we be dear to you among the gods as we sing your praises.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, this Sūrya, the beholder of men, rises over both worlds upon the earth;

he is the guardian of all that is stationary and all that moves, perceiving the straight among mortals and discerning the crooked. He has harnessed from their station the seven bay mares, dripping with clarity, who carry Sūrya.
Devoted to you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa, he who beholds all living beings as if they were herds [of cattle] reaches your abodes.
Your nourishing, honey-sweet offerings have risen up; Sūrya has ascended the bright ocean.
For him, the Ādityas—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa acting in harmony—prepare his paths.
These are indeed the discerners of abundant falsehood—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa.
They have been magnified in the dwelling-place of Ṛta; they are the capable sons of Aditi, invincible.
These Mitra and Varuṇa, who are difficult to deceive, awaken even the mindless with their insights.
Even while they perform their well-intentioned rite, they lead [the worshipper] across sin by a good path.
These [gods], who do not close their eyes, who are mindful of heaven and earth, lead the thoughtless one [to safety].
Even in the desert there is a ford in the rivers; may they carry us across this perilous strait.

RV 7.60.8.1–2: That auspicious protection which Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, like guardians, extend to Sudās—placing our children and grandchildren within it, O swift ones, let us not commit any offense against the gods.
RV 7.60.9.1: Let him worship at the altar with oblations; may he ward off whatever snares of Varuṇa there may be.
May Aryaman ward off our enemies; O Bulls, grant wide space to Sudās!
For even this encounter is hidden from them, yet they prevail by secret power. O Bulls, trembling with fear of you, show us mercy through the greatness of Dakṣa!

He who offers his devotion to the sacred word (*brahman*) for the sake of winning booty and the highest wealth—those liberal patrons strive against the wrath of the enemy; they have prepared a wide and well-established dwelling for their habitation.
O divine Mitra and Varuṇa, this priestly service has been performed for you both at the sacrifices.
Carry us across all difficulties; do you protect us always with blessings.
The eye of you two gods, O Varuṇa and Mitra, the beautiful countenance of Sūrya, rises up, spreading its light.
He who beholds all beings has taken notice of the fury among mortals.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this inspired singer, faithful to the *ṛta*, offers you prayers that reach far; whose sacred hymns (*brahmāṇi*) you two, O wise ones, protect, so that through his wisdom you may fulfill the autumns. O Mitra and Varuṇa, givers of good gifts, [you have risen] from the wide earth and from the lofty, vast heaven.
You two establish your spies among the plants and among the people, moving separately, guarding with unblinking eyes.
I praise the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa; their impetuous might has firmly established the two worlds by its greatness.
May the months of those who do not sacrifice pass away without heroes; may he who meditates on the sacrifice extend his own stronghold.
O all-pervading bulls, these [sacrificial offerings] of yours are unerring; in them no wondrous marvel has been seen.
The deceptions and falsehoods of men attend upon us, yet no secrets have remained hidden from you two.
With prostrations I magnify your sacrifice together; I invoke you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with earnest entreaty.
I proclaim new hymns for you both to sing; may these prayers offered by us be pleasing to you.
O God, this is our priestly service...
The Sun has sent forth his lofty rays over all the many generations of men.
Shining like heaven, he has become visible; fashioned by his makers with wisdom, he has become well-fashioned.
O Sūrya, come forth toward us with these hymns, with your coursers Etaśas as your steeds. Proclaim us sinless before Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and Agni.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the upholders of cosmic order—grant us thousands of spoils.
May the radiant ones bestow upon us our highest hymn of praise; may they, being lauded, fulfill our desire.
O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, protect us—you who were born of noble lineage from those sublime progenitors.
May we not incur the wrath of Varuṇa or Vāyu, nor that of Mitra, the most beloved among men.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with ghee.
O youthful ones, make us famous among the people; hear, O Mitra and Varuṇa, these my invocations.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant wide space for ourselves and for our offspring. May all our paths be easy to traverse and well-trodden. Do you protect us always with blessings.
The fortunate Sūrya, who beholds all, rises up as the common property of all mankind.
The god who, like a skin, has rolled up the darkness—the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa—rises up.
The great banner of Sūrya, the surging wave that impels men, rises up. He who, yoked to the pole, draws Etaśa as he seeks to turn the common wheel.
Radiant from the lap of the dawns, he rises up being celebrated by the singers;
this god Savitṛ is my delight, who does not violate his common law.
The golden ornament of heaven, far-seeing, he rises with his goal afar, crossing over, shining brightly.
Surely, impelled by Sūrya, men go forth to their goals and perform their labors;
where the immortals have made a path for him, he follows that course like a falcon swooping down.
At the rising of the sun, we shall worship you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, with reverences and oblations.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman...
Dwelling in heaven over the mid-air and upon the earth, may they spread out for you the bright coverings of clarified butter.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and the well-born King Varuṇa of noble power graciously accept our oblation.
O two kings, guardians of the great *ṛta*, lords of the rivers, Kṣatriyas, come hither!
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who grant quickening gifts, send down from heaven our nourishment and rain!
May the god Mitra, Varuṇa, and the noble Aryaman lead us forward by the most effective paths.
Speak so that we may be honored; may we rejoice in nourishment together with Sudās, protected by the gods.

He who has fashioned this chariot-seat for you both in his mind, and who shall make and maintain this upright prayer— Sprinkle it with clarity, O Mitra and Varuṇa; as kings, satisfy those well-settled lands.

RV 7.64.5: This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered to you like bright Soma to Vāyu. Favour our prayers, awaken our inspirations; protect us evermore with your blessings! RV 7.65.1: At the rising of the sun, I call upon you both with well-spoken hymns—Mitra and Varuṇa of pure intent.
Those two, whose divine power is undecaying and supreme, who are honored at the movement of all that moves;
for they are the two Asuras among the gods, the most powerful—may you two make our dwellings full of vigor.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we attain you both where the heavens and the days overflow with abundance.
They are the two bridges of falsehood with many snares, difficult for the mortal enemy to cross.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we cross over misfortunes by the path of *ṛta* (cosmic order), as one crosses waters with a boat.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, come to our enjoyment of the oblation; sprinkle our pasture with clarified butter and with refreshing offerings.
Bestow here upon the people a choice portion of your favor; grant us a share of the delightful water of heaven.
This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra...
Let this vigorous hymn go forth to Mitra and Varuṇa.
The worshipper [praises] the two of mighty birth,
those who, highly skilled and great in power, were sustained by the gods for the sake of divine dominion, O you whose father is Dakṣa.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you who protect our bodies and guard us from harm, fulfill the prayers of those who sing your praises.
When today, at the rising of the sun, Mitra and Aryaman [declare us] sinless...
Savitar shall impel Bhaga; may that dwelling be well-protected. Now, O bounteous ones, proceed on your journey, you who carry us across distress.
And [I praise] the self-ruling Aditi and those two kings who rule over the great, infallible ordinance.
At the rising of the sun, I sing in praise of you both, Mitra and Varuṇa.
To Aryaman, the destroyer of enemies;
with wealth of gold, may this prayer [be offered] for unassailable power; may this inspired singer [pray] for the winning of the prize.
May we be yours, O divine Varuṇa, and yours, O Mitra, together with our patrons; may we obtain nourishment and well-being.
Many are they who have the sun as their eye, Agni as their tongue, and who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).

They who, by their insights, have directed the three assemblies with all-encompassing powers; they who have established the year, the month, and the day, as well as the sacrifice, the oblation, and the verse— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, these kings, have attained an unattainable sovereignty.
This we meditate upon for you today with hymns at the rising of the sun, so that Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman may grant us [favor]. You are the charioteers of *ṛta*.
You who abide in *ṛta*, born of *ṛta*, who increase *ṛta*—terrible ones, haters of untruth.
O heroes, may we and those who are our wise patrons abide in your most gracious favor, which provides the best protection. That beautiful form rises up at the turning point of heaven,
which the swift divine steed Etaśa draws, sufficient for all to behold.
The Lord of all that moves and stands, who traverses the entire mid-air;
seven sisters, the bay mares, carry Sūrya in his chariot for our prosperity.
That bright eye, established by the gods, has risen upward.
May we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns. O undeceivable Varuṇa, come with your poetic wisdom, O radiant one, and Mitra, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, come with the splendors of heaven, you who are free from guile;
drink the Soma that bestows vital strength.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, heroes, come hither, graciously accepting our oblation.
Drink the Soma, O you who increase the cosmic order!
O two lords of men, I approach your chariot with a sacrificial mind, full of oblations, to celebrate you— I, who have awakened you like a messenger, call out to you as a son calls to his parents.
The fire has been kindled among us, free from sorrow; even the ends of darkness have become visible.
The banner of the Dawn has appeared in the east, born for the glory of the Daughter of Heaven.
Now, O Aśvins, Nāsatyas, the eloquent and skillful invoker attends upon you both with hymns of praise.
Come hither by many ancient paths on your light-finding, treasure-laden chariot.
O Aśvins, I, your devoted servant, now call upon you both for the pressed juice, seeking wealth, O lovers of sweetness.
Let your sturdy horses carry you hither; drink among us the well-pressed honeyed draughts.

O divine Aśvins, turn my forward-striving prayer toward you; make it unfailing so that we may win wealth. Protect us in all our strengths and in the abundance of our thoughts; O Lords of Power, assist us with your powers.
O Aśvins, protect us in these prayers of ours; may our seed be prolific and free from shame.

RV 7.67.6: Striving for offspring and progeny, we, possessing fine jewels, would go to the feast of the gods, [O Aśvins]. RV 7.67.7: This treasure has been placed for you two, like one set aside for friendship in the past; O lovers of sweetness, it is granted to us.
Come hither with a mind free from anger, eating the oblation among the human clans.
In a single course, O active ones, upon the same path, your chariot has gone around the seven flowing rivers.
The well-born steeds, yoked by the gods, do not weary as they pull with speed at your poles.
Be inexhaustible for the sake of the liberal patrons who, with their wealth, incite the giving of riches.
RV_07.067.09.2: Those who extend their kinship through noble gifts (*sūnṛtā*), bestowing wealth in cattle and horses;
RV_07.067.10.1: Now hear my invocation, O youthful ones! Come, O Aśvins, upon your path rich in light. RV_07.067.10.2:
Bestow treasures and grant long life to our patrons. Protect us always with your blessings.
Come hither, O radiant Aśvins, with your noble horses, you wonder-workers who take pleasure in the songs of your devotee.
Accept our oblations that have been presented; enjoy them.
The exhilarating juices have been set forth; come quickly to partake of my offering.
Hear our invocations even beyond those of the noble one.
O Aśvins, your chariot, swift as thought and possessing a hundred aids, speeds forth across the regions for us, you who possess the wealth of Sūryā.
When this stone, seeking the gods, presses upward for you both, the Soma-presser speaking aloud for your sake— may the inspired singer turn you, the beautiful ones, hither with oblations.
For that wondrous nourishment which you possess, bestow it now upon Atri, rich in buffaloes.
He who, being dear, bestows the gift of wisdom;
and that same [favor] was yours, O Aśvins, for Cyavāna as he grew old, when you, O givers of oblations,
bestowed upon him a form surpassing this [present one].

And those evil-minded friends abandoned that Bhujyu, O Aśvins, in the middle of the ocean; you rescued him, he who was devoted to you. You gave aid even to Vṛka when he was being devoured, and you were heard by Śayu as he called upon you.
RV_07.068.08.2 As you two caused the cow to swell with milk like waters, O Aśvins, even the barren one was made fertile through your powers and skillful deeds.
RV_07.068.09.1 This very singer, well-disposed in mind, awakens at the forefront of the dawns with his hymns of praise.
RV_07.068.09.2 May the cow increase him with nourishment and with milk; and may you protect us always with blessings.
May your golden chariot, pressing against heaven and earth, come hither with its stallions;
gleaming with fellies, its path anointed with ghee, it is the bearer of refreshments, the lord of men, rich in prize-winning steeds.
May that chariot, spreading itself over the five regions, with three seats and yoked by thought, approach us.
By which you go to the people who seek the gods, O Aśvins, taking whatever course you choose;
come hither with your noble horses, O glorious ones, and drink from the honeyed treasure, O wonder-workers.
Your chariot, speeding with your bride, presses against the ends of heaven by its two tracks.
The Daughter of the Sun chose your splendor for herself during the night’s departure;
when you two, with your powers, protect the one who seeks the gods, your bird-like vigor goes around the heat with joy.
O chariot-borne ones, that very chariot of yours, harnessed at dawn, travels its circuitous path.
With that, O Aśvins, bring us peace and well-being at the dawning of the Uṣas; bring us to this sacrifice.
O Heroes, like thirsty bulls seeking lightning, come today to our libation.
For men invoke you from many places with their prayers; let not other seekers of the gods detain you.
You two carried Bhujyu, who was cast down into the ocean, out from the waters with your unfailing,
winged steeds— unwearied, unshakable, and wondrous— O Aśvins, bringing him across.
Now, O youthful ones, hear my invocation!
O Aśvins, possessors of all boons, come to us! That station of yours upon the earth has been proclaimed.
Like a prize-winning horse with a swift back, you have taken your seat as if upon a fixed womb.
That most excellent benevolence of yours attends us; even the heated offering (gharma) is present within the dwelling of man.
He who brings you across the oceans and rivers, yoking even the well-yoked steeds that move like birds;

Whatever places you two, O Aśvins, establish—among the great waters of heaven, in the plants, or among the people; Or when you sit upon the summit of the mountain—you bring nourishment to the person who offers oblations.
O Gods, you have taken delight in the plants and in the waters, when you, as the objects of the seers' devotion, attained your purpose.
Bestowing many treasures upon us, you have looked back over the ancient ages.
Though you have already heard much, O Aśvins, you still behold the many prayers of the seers.
Come forth to the chosen man; may your most excellent benevolence be with us.
O Nāsatyas, may that sacrifice of his which is accompanied by oblations and prepared with sacred hymns be successful in the assembly.
Come forth to the chosen Vasiṣṭha; these prayers are being recited for you both.

RV_07.070.07.1 This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins; O Bulls, may you take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn. RV_07.070.07.2 These prayers, longing for you, have gone forth; do you protect us always with blessings.
RV_07.071.01.1 The sister Dawn departs from her sister Night; the dark one yields the path to the ruddy one.
O givers of horses, givers of cattle, we invoke you; day and night, keep the arrow away from us.
Come to the mortal who offers oblations, O Aśvins, bringing desirable wealth upon your chariot.
Drive away from us lack of food and disease; O lovers of sweetness, protect us by day and by night.
May the bulls, seeking your favor, bring your chariot hither at the earliest flush of dawn.

O Aśvins, with horses yoked by the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), bring your treasure-laden chariot, its reins held firmly in hand. That chariot of yours, O lords of men, which is the bearer [of gifts], three-seated, wealthy, and swift as the rays of light—[bring that here].
Come to us with these, O Nāsatyas, for that which brings all-sustaining wealth approaches you.
You released Cyavāna from old age; you brought the swift horse to Pedu.
You delivered Atri from distress and darkness, and you placed Jāhuṣa within a secure dwelling.
This is the inspired thought, this is the song for you, O Aśvins. Come, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot rich in cattle, rich in horses, and full of manifold splendor!
All our teams attend upon you, as you shine with desirable beauty in your very bodies.
Come toward us with the gods, O Nāsatyas, being of one accord on your chariot;
for our friendship with you is ancestral, our kinship is common—be mindful of that.
The hymns of praise for the Aśvins have awakened, as have the kinship prayers and the divine Dawns.
Seeking to win over the two worlds, the inspired sage addresses these two divine ones, O Nāsatyas.
When the dawns shine forth, O Aśvins, the poets bring their sacred prayers to you.
The god Savitṛ has sent his light upward; the great fires sing out in praise with their fuel.
O Nāsatyas, come from behind; O Aśvins, come from the front, from below, and from above!
Come from every side with wealth that belongs to the five peoples! Do you protect us always with blessings!
We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness, offering our hymn of praise as we seek the gods.
The song invokes the Aśvins, the doers of many deeds, the most frequent visitors, the ancient and immortal ones.
The dear Hotṛ-priest of man has sat down, O Nāsatyas, he who sacrifices and offers praise.
Eat of the sweetness, O Aśvins, nearby; I, providing the sacrificial food, call you to the assemblies.
We have offered the sacrifice, following the paths of the gods; O Bulls, may you take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn.
Like one sent with a ready ear, Vasiṣṭha has awakened you with his praises as he sings your glory.
May those two bearers come to our people, O slayers of demons, joined together, with firm hands.
The exhilarating draughts have come together; do not neglect us, but come with auspicious favor.
From behind and from the front, O Nāsatyas...
These morning sacrifices call upon you both, O Aśvins, at the break of dawn.
I invoke you both for aid, O lords of power, for you go to every tribe.
O heroes, you bestow wondrous nourishment; impel it toward him who possesses the truth.
With one mind, turn your chariot hither and draw near; drink the sweet Soma juice.
Come hither, attend to us, and drink of the honeyed draught, O Aśvins!
O bulls, you who possess noble wealth, drink the milk that has been milked; do not neglect us, but come to us! The horses that carry you fly toward the house of the donor, bearing you both.
O Aśvins, O divine heroes, come quickly with your swift horses, showing favor to us.
Then, as they go forth, O Aśvins, the wise patrons shall attend to you for nourishment.
May those Nāsatyas grant lasting glory and a secure dwelling to our generous patrons, and to us as well.
Those who have gone forth like chariots, free from malice, protectors of men;
those heroes have increased by their own power and dwell in secure habitation.
Dawn, born of heaven, has shone forth according to the cosmic order (ṛta), manifesting her majesty.
The most excellent one has driven away the darkness and the enemies; the best of the Aṅgirases has awakened the paths.
Awaken us today for great prosperity; O Dawn, lead us toward great good fortune.
Bestow upon us, O divine and human goddess, wonderful wealth, glorious and renowned among mortals.
These, those radiant beams of the beautiful Dawn, the immortal ones, have come;
engendering the divine ordinances and filling the mid-air, they have spread abroad.
This very one, yoking herself from afar, swiftly traverses the five lands.
Beholding the works of men, the Daughter of Heaven, the mistress of the world—
rich in steeds, the bride of Sūrya, possessing wondrous wealth, she rules over riches.
Praised by the seers, awakening the world, the bountiful Dawn shines forth, extolled by the priests.
The bright, ruddy horses, radiant with light, have become visible as they carry the Dawn;
she comes, resplendent and adorned with every ornament upon her chariot, bestowing treasure upon the person who honors her.
True with the true, great with the great, the goddess is worthy of sacrifice among the gods, and holy among those worthy of worship.
Breaking through the firm [enclosures], he gave up the cows; the cattle lowed toward the Dawn.
Now, O Dawn, bestow upon us wealth consisting of cattle, heroes, horses, and much nourishment.
Do not let our sacrificial grass be subject to reproach among men; protect us always with your blessings.
Upward has Savitṛ, the god who belongs to all men, extended the immortal light that is common to all.
Through the power of the gods, the Eye was born; Uṣas has made the entire world manifest.
The paths leading to the gods have appeared before me—paths that do not fail, prepared by the Vasus.
The banner of the Dawn has appeared in the east; she has come hither from the mansions.
Those were indeed many days that lay behind the sun when it rose in the east, since you, O Dawn, have been seen moving like a lover, not like one who returns.
They were the companions at the feast of the gods, the truth-abiding seers of old.
The fathers found the hidden light; with true mantras, they brought forth the Dawn.
Meeting together in the same enclosure, they are in harmony; they do not strive against one another.
They do not violate the laws of the gods, being unharmed and moving in harmony with the Vasus.
The Vasiṣṭhas, waking at dawn, praise you with hymns, O auspicious one, having offered their laudations.
Leader of the cattle, mistress of booty, shine forth for us; O nobly born Dawn, be the first to awaken.
This leader of wealth, this Dawn, shining forth with her true words, is praised by the Vasiṣṭhas as she bestows upon us far-famed riches. Preserve us evermore with blessings!
Like a young maiden, she has shone forth, inciting every living being to go about its work.
Agni has appeared for the kindling of men; he has made light, driving away the darkness.
Facing all things, she has risen wide-expanding, wearing a radiant garment; she has shone white and bright.
Golden-colored, beautiful to behold, the mother of the cows, the leader of the days, has gleamed.
The blessed Dawn, the eye of the gods, comes bearing the white horse, beautiful to behold;
she has appeared, distinguished by her rays, bringing wondrous wealth, spreading over all.
Driving away the enemy near at hand and far away, O wide one, grant us pasture free from fear.
Drive away our enemies; bring us riches; impel bounty toward the one who praises you, O generous lady!
Shine forth for us with your most excellent beams, O divine Dawn, prolonging our lifespan.
Bestowing nourishment upon us, O possessor of all boons, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, and chariots.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, well-born one, whom the Vasiṣṭhas magnify with their hymns—you, bestow upon us lofty and vast wealth! And may you all protect us evermore!
Her first rays have become visible; her bright colors spread upward.
O Dawn, on your lofty, radiant chariot, bring desirable wealth toward us. The kindled fire awakens to greet her; the sages, singing with their hymns, welcome her.
Dawn approaches, the goddess who drives away all darkness and misfortunes with her light.
These very Dawns have appeared in the east, bestowing light as they shine forth.
They have brought forth the sun, the sacrifice, and Agni; the hated darkness has departed to the west.
The wealthy Daughter of Heaven has become visible; all behold the shining Dawn.
He has mounted the chariot that is harnessed by its own power; the well-yoked horses carry it forward.
Today our benevolent ones have awakened toward you—our liberal patrons and we ourselves. O Dawns, shine forth with your radiance; do you protect us always with blessings.
Dawn has revealed the paths of men, awakening the five human tribes.
With her well-beheld bulls she has sent forth her light; Sūrya has opened heaven and earth with his vision.
She manifests her rays at the ends of heaven; the Dawns strive like people who have harnessed their teams.
Your rays roll up the darkness; they extend the light like Savitṛ extends his arms.
Dawn has become most Indra-like, the munificent one; she has brought forth glories for our well-being.
The goddess, daughter of heaven, bestows treasures upon the doer of good deeds—she who is most like an Aṅgiras.
O Dawn, grant us that wealth which you bestowed upon those who praised you when you were lauded;
you whom they brought forth with the roar of the bull, you opened the doors of the firm mountain.
Impelling every god toward bounty, she sends forth our true and pleasant speech.
Shining forth, bestow upon us the inspiration for the winning of gain. And may you protect us always with blessings. With hymns and songs, the wise Vasiṣṭhas have awakened first to greet the Dawn.
She who turns the two regions that meet at their ends, making all living beings manifest.
Bestowing new life upon us, Uṣas has awakened, having hidden the darkness with light.
The youthful maiden goes forth unabashed; she has made manifest the sun, the sacrifice, and Agni.
May our Dawns come rich in horses and cattle...
The daughter of Heaven has been seen approaching, rising up;
she uncovers the waters so that we may see, and the noble lady creates light to dispel the darkness.
Rising together with the sun, he releases the bright rays; as he ascends, the radiant star shines forth.
O Uṣas, at your dawning and that of the sun, may we attain our share.
O Daughter of Heaven, O Uṣas, we have awakened for you, the swift one,
you who bring much-desired wealth, O bountiful one, like a treasure, joy to the donor.

O Great Goddess, shining forth, you who by your greatness create splendor for us to behold, O you who look upon the light of heaven—we pray for a share of those jewels of yours; may we be like sons unto a mother.
O Dawn, bring that wondrous bounty which is most renowned from afar.
O Daughter of Heaven, grant us that which is the sustenance of mortals; may we enjoy it.
Bestow immortal glory upon our patrons, and upon us, wealth consisting of cattle and vigorous strength.
May Uṣas, the impeller of the wealthy and full of pleasant truths, dawn away our enemies.
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant great protection for our sacrifice to our people and our kin.
May we overcome the evil-minded who attack us, even those who persist in their hostility for a long time.
One of you is called the sovereign ruler, the other the self-ruling lord; O Indra and Varuṇa, you two are great and possessors of great wealth.
All the gods in the highest heaven, O mighty ones, have bestowed upon you united vigor and strength.
With power, you have pierced the channels of the waters and set the sun in the sky as its lord.
O Indra and Varuṇa, in the exhilaration of this [soma], you two have caused the waters to swell; O masters of wondrous power, cause our prayers to swell.
In battles and in conflicts, the priests bring you both forward; for the attainment of security, those with firm-kneed steeds call upon you both.
O poets, we invoke the easily-invoked Indra and Varuṇa, the lords of both kinds of wealth.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when you two created all these beings of the world by your own power,
Mitra honors Varuṇa with peace, while the fierce one, eager for glory, moves along with the Maruts. For the sake of Varuṇa’s great prize, they two measure out his own steadfast splendor and strength.
One strikes down the unrelated foe who seeks to harm; the other, with few, overcomes the many.

Neither distress, nor misfortunes, nor affliction from any quarter reaches that mortal, O Indra and Varuṇa, to whose sacrifice you two, O Gods, go and enjoy; upon him no treacherous assault of a mortal falls.
Come hither, O heroes, with divine protection; hear my call if you take pleasure in it.
For you two, Indra and Varuṇa, bestow your friendship, your kinship, and your compassion.
O Indra and Varuṇa, in battle after battle, be our warriors in the front, you who possess the strength of the peoples.
When both sides call upon you in the heat of competition, O heroes, for the winning of sons and grandsons;
may Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us glory and great, far-reaching protection.
We meditate upon the unfailing light of Aditi, who increases the Truth, and upon the hymn of the divine Savitṛ.
Beholding you two, O heroes, as their kin, men seeking cattle with broad axes have marched forward.
O Indra and Varuṇa, with your protection, slay both the Dāsa and the Ārya enemies, and aid Sudās.
Where men gather together with raised banners, in that battle where there is something dear to win—there may you stand.
RV 7.83.2: Where the world-protectors who behold the light of heaven are afraid, there, O Indra and Varuṇa, speak for us.
RV 7.83.3: The dark ends of the earth have become visible; O Indra and Varuṇa, the cry has ascended to heaven.
The hostilities of the people have come near to me; come hither with your protection, you who hear our invocation!
O Indra and Varuṇa, with your irresistible weapons, you who conquer Bheda, protect Sudās.
Hear their prayers at the invocation; the priestly service of the Tṛtsus has proven true.
O Indra and Varuṇa, the hostilities of the enemy and the enmities of our rivals oppress me.
For you two rule over the wealth of both worlds; therefore, protect us on the decisive day.
Both sides invoke you two in the battles—Indra and Varuṇa—for the winning of wealth, when you protected Sudās together with the Tṛtsus, who were hard-pressed by ten kings.
Ten kings, having come together, though they were unrighteous, did not prevail against Sudās, O Indra and Varuṇa.
The praise of these men who sit at the feast was true; the gods were present at their invocations.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow your aid upon Sudās, who was surrounded on all sides in the battle of the ten kings.

Where the Tṛtsus, white-robed and wearing their hair in braids, have worshipped with homage and prayerful thought, one of you slays the Vṛtras in battles, while the other ever protects the sacred laws. We invoke you both, O mighty ones, with well-fashioned hymns; O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us your protection.
May Indra, Varuṇa, and Mitra [be] with us...
O Kings, Indra and Varuṇa, may I turn you both hither to the sacrifice with oblations and salutations.
The ladle filled with clarified butter, held in our arms, goes forth by itself toward you who possess diverse forms.
The vast realm of you two is impelled by heaven, you who bind with fetters that require no ropes.
May you spare us from the wrath of Varuṇa; may Indra make for us a wide space.
Make our sacrifice dear in the assemblies; make our prayers praised among the patrons.
May wealth impelled by the gods come near to us; may he further us with his desirable aids.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon us wealth containing all boons, rich in treasures and abundant in food.
He who, as the Āditya, destroys falsehoods—that hero distributes boundless riches.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa; may it protect us, striving for strength in our children and descendants.
Possessing fine jewels, may we go to the feast of the gods. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings. I purify for you both, Indra and Varuṇa, a thought free from demons, offering Soma.
Like the goddess Dawn whose face is anointed with ghee, may those two protect us on their journey in the encounter.
Indeed, they vie with one another here at the invocation of the gods, while the arrows fall upon those banners.
O Indra and Varuṇa, strike those enemies back with your shaft, scattering them in all directions.
Even the Waters, goddesses glorious in their own splendor, have established Indra and Varuṇa as deities in their assemblies.
One of them sustains the scattered peoples; the other slays the irresistible Vṛtras.
Let him be the wise and truth-perceiving Hotṛ-priest, who, through his power, bows down to you both, O Ādityas.
May he who possesses the oblation and offers the sacrificial food turn you both toward us for our protection, so that we may attain prosperity.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa...
The wise one, by his greatness, has indeed propped apart the generations and the two wide worlds.
He has pushed up the lofty, vast vault of heaven; he has twice spread out the starry firmament and the earth.
And I converse with him regarding that very body of mine: "When indeed shall I be within the reach of Varuṇa?
What offering of mine will he accept without anger? When shall I look upon his grace with a well-disposed mind?"
I ask about that sin, O Varuṇa, desiring to see it; I approach you, the wise one, with my inquiry.
Even the seers have told me this in common: "This Varuṇa is angry with you.
What was the greatest transgression, O Varuṇa, that you seek to strike down your own praiser, your friend?
Proclaim this for me, O hard-to-overcome one, self-dependent one! May I quickly approach you with sinless homage.
Release us from the sins committed by our fathers, and from those which we ourselves have committed with our own bodies.
O King, release Vasiṣṭha like a thief who has stolen cattle, or like a calf from its tether.

RV 7.86.6.1: That is not one's own skill, O Varuṇa; it is deception, intoxication, wrath, the die, and thoughtlessness. RV 7.86.6.2: The elder exists upon the surface of the younger; even sleep itself is the dispeller of untruth. RV 7.86.7.1: Like a servant, may I, being sinless, do what is sufficient for the impetuous god who has bestowed his bounty.
The wise god has enlightened the unwise; the more inspired poet impels the skillful man toward wealth.
O self-dependent Varuṇa, may this hymn of praise be firmly established in your heart.
May there be well-being for us in rest and success for us in exertion. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.

Varuṇa carved out paths for the sun and opened the oceanic channels of the rivers. Like a released troop of mares, he, following the cosmic order (*ṛta*), set the great waters flowing toward the days. The wind, your breath, has roared through the mid-air like a restless beast that has found pasture.
Within these two great worlds, the vast heaven and earth, all your dear domains are established, O Varuṇa.
The spies of Varuṇa, sent forth at his command, survey both well-fashioned worlds.
The seers who abide in Truth, wise in sacrifice, and possessed of foresight, have extended their inspired hymns.
Varuṇa spoke to me, the wise one: "The Cow bears twenty-one names.
Knowing the secret places of the foot, the sage did not proclaim them, desiring to instruct a later generation.
Three heavens are deposited within him; three earths are above, forming six divisions.
The skillful King Varuṇa has fashioned this golden swing in heaven for his glory. Like a drop, like a white deer, the mighty Varuṇa stands over the river;
he whose proclamation is deep, the measurer of the mid-world, the king of this existing order, possesses a kingdom that brings us safely across.
May he who shows mercy even to one who has committed an offense grant that we remain sinless before Varuṇa.
Fulfilling the ordinances of Aditi, may you protect us evermore.
O Vasiṣṭha, present to the bounteous Varuṇa this most beloved hymn, as pure as a stream.
He who brings hither the worshipful one, the thousandfold, the bull, the great;
Then, having come into his sight, I deem the face of Agni to be that of Varuṇa.
When the heavenly lord has brought the plant upon the stone, may he lead me toward the form for beholding.
When Varuṇa and I mounted the boat and we propelled it into the midst of the ocean;
when we moved over the ridges of the waters, let us swing upon the swing for our glory.
Varuṇa, the skillful worker, has indeed established Vasiṣṭha on the boat and made him a seer through his mighty powers.
The sage is the praiser on the days of fair weather—those very days that the heavens and the dawns have extended. Where has our former friendship gone, when we once dwelt together in safety?
O self-dependent Varuṇa, I have entered your lofty dwelling, your house with a thousand doors.

O Varuṇa, if a constant friend and beloved comrade should commit offenses against you, O Sage, let us not suffer for his sins, O Lord of Sacrifice; grant protection to him who praises you. While we dwell in these secure habitations, may Varuṇa release the bond from us.
Seeking aid from the lap of Aditi—do you all protect us!
O King Varuṇa, may I not go to a house made of clay;
have mercy, O good ruler, have mercy!

When I go forth, O wielder of the stone, quivering like an inflated leather bag, have mercy on me, O pure one! Indeed, through the deficiency of my mental power, I have gone against you, O radiant one.
Be gracious, O Soma,
be gracious. To the singer who, standing in the midst of the waters, was overcome by thirst—
be gracious, O Soma, be gracious.
Whatever offense we humans may commit against the divine host, O Varuṇa,
whether through thoughtlessness or by violating your laws— O God, do not harm us for that sin. The pure,
honey-sweet pressed juices have been offered to you both with the skill of the *adhvaryu*s, accompanied by heroic songs.
O Vāyu, bring your teams; come hither to drink the pressed juice for exhilaration.
To you, O Vāyu, who are the Lord, he who has offered the oblation—pure Soma for you, the drinker of the pure— makes him renowned among mortals; every son born of him is born as a victor.
For the sake of wealth, these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, brought him forth; for the sake of wealth, the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god.
And may his teams attend upon Vāyu, and also the white one, the bestower of treasures, in the highest place.
The Uṣases have dawned with auspicious days, stainless; reflecting, they have found the wide light.
The Usijs have opened up even the stall of cattle; for them, from days of old, the waters have flowed.
They, meditating with a truthful mind, carry [the chariot] yoked by their own will. O Indra and Vāyu, lords of all, the nourishments attend your hero-bearing chariot.
Those who are lords and bestow heaven upon us with cattle, horses, riches, and gold—
Indra and Vāyu, may those wise patrons overcome all enemies in battles with their chariot-horses and heroes.
Like coursers seeking glory, we Vasiṣṭhas entreat Indra and Vāyu with our excellent hymns.

Seeking booty for our protection, let us invoke you; do you protect us always with your blessings. Indeed, those blameless gods who of old were strengthened by our homage—those very ones made the dawn shine with the sun for Vāyu and for Manu when he was oppressed.
Desiring [us], like two messengers, as guardians not to be deceived, you protect us through many months and autumns.
O Indra and Vāyu, our excellent praise approaches you; it seeks your compassion and new-found prosperity.
The wise one, white-hued and the glory of his teams of horses, attends those whose food is fat and who increase their wealth.
They have stood forth with one mind for Vāyu; all the men have performed noble deeds.

As far as the strength of their bodies extends, as far as their vigor, and as far as the men can perceive with their sight—O Indra and Vāyu, drinkers of the pure, drink the pure Soma for us; sit here upon this sacred grass.

Harnessing your teams of horses that bring desirable heroes, O Indra and Vāyu, come hither toward us; for this foremost portion of the sweet mead has been presented for you both. Now, being gratified, release [the steeds] for us.

O Indra and Vāyu, those hundred teams and those thousand of yours, which follow you as possessors of all boons—come hither with those well-disposed teams! O Heroes, drink of the sweet mead that has been offered.
Like coursers for glory...
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come to us; a thousand are your teams, O you who possess all boons.
I offer to you the intoxicating juice, of which you, O God, have the first draught.
The swift presser has stepped forth at the sacrifices so that Indra and Vāyu may drink the Soma.
When the god-seeking Adhvaryus bring the first of the sweet mead for you both with their skillful acts,
O Vāyu, come hither with your teams of horses to the giver of oblations in his dwelling, that you may enjoy it.
Bestow upon us wealth that provides excellent nourishment; grant us heroic sons and the bounty of cattle and horses.

May we, together with our patrons, be those who gladden Indra like the winds, who are god-seeking, victorious, and noble; may we, slaying the obstructors, be conquerors in battle against our enemies through our heroes.
RV_07.092.05.1 Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands, to this ritual.
O Vāyu, rejoice at this libation! [And may you gods protect us always with blessings.
RV_07.093.01.1 Today, O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, graciously accept this pure hymn newly born.
For I invoke you both, who are easily summoned; may you two most swiftly grant strength to him who desires it.
For you two have become winners of booty, powerful and growing together, increasing in might.
Ruling over abundant wealth and pasture, bestow upon us a full measure of enduring and vigorous strength.
When the inspired singers, seeking favor with their prayers,
come near the assembly like swift steeds reaching the goal, those men invoke Indra and Agni.
With songs, the inspired singer, seeking favor, implores for glorious wealth that brings the first share.
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fair thunderbolt, further us with new gifts.

When the two great ones, contending and vying with each other, radiant in their own bodies, come together for the battle of heroes; then, at the sacrifice, you utterly strike down the godless man by means of the god-loving people who press the Soma.
O Indra and Agni, come hither to this very pressing of Soma for our goodwill. For you do not disregard us at all; may I turn you toward me with constant offerings of strength.
O Agni, kindled by this homage, speak forth to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra.
Whatever offense we have committed against Sīman, may Aryaman and Aditi forgive that; may they loosen it.
O Agni, seeking your protection, may we, together with you both, attain these offerings and strengths.
May Indra, Viṣṇu, and the Maruts not overlook us. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
O Indra and Agni, this ancient praise of yours has arisen from my mind like rain from a cloud.
O Indra and Agni, hear the call of the singer; accept our songs.
O Lords, nourish our inspired thoughts. O Indra and Agni, lords of men, do not deliver us to misfortune, nor to calumny;
do not leave us exposed to reproach.
To Indra and Agni we offer great homage and a well-fashioned hymn; with prayer and song, seeking aid, we implore them.
For indeed, the sages ever invoke them thus for their protection.
Together with our companions, for the winning of the prize;
we, praising you with songs and offering oblations, invoke you both,
desiring to win at the sacrifice.
O Indra and Agni, you who subdue the peoples, come to us with your protection.
Let not the one of evil intent have power over us. Let not the malice of any stingy mortal reach us.
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection! O Indra and Agni, may we win that wealth which we implore from you—wealth consisting of cattle, gold, and horses.
O Indra and Agni, may we obtain that.
When, O Soma, the men have pressed you out, they have called upon Indra and Agni;
The worshipful ones, possessing steeds,
[call] with hymns those two greatest slayers of Vṛtra, Who, even when exhilarated, are moved by our song.
With hymns of praise, seek to win them over.
Slay with your blow that mortal who speaks evil and is ill-disposed, the sorcerer; slay him with your blow, as one strikes down a serpent in the water.
With her swelling flood and nourishing power, this Sarasvatī has flowed forth—a supporting fortress of iron.
Like a chariot, she advances, pushing aside all other rivers by her greatness.
Sarasvatī alone among the rivers has taken notice, as she flows pure from the mountains to the ocean.
Awakening wealth for the world’s abundance, she has yielded milk and clarified butter for the descendant of Nahuṣa.
He has grown strong among the women—manly, a bull, a vigorous youth among those worthy of sacrifice.
He bestows swift vigor upon the patrons; may he cleanse his own body for the sake of winning booty.

And may Sarasvatī, the auspicious one, hear us with favor at this sacrifice; coming with her measured steps, to be honored by those who bow down, she is superior to our friends through her alliance with wealth.
O Sarasvatī, accept this hymn with favor from us, who offer these oblations with our salutations.
Placing ourselves under your most beloved protection, may we take refuge in you as [one takes shelter] beneath a tree.
O Sarasvatī, O blessed one, this Vasiṣṭha has opened for you the two doors of Cosmic Order (ṛta). Prosper, O radiant one;
grant spoils of war to the one who praises you. And do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
I sing forth a lofty song for her who possesses the power of the rivers;
O Vasiṣṭha, with well-fashioned hymns and praises, magnify Sarasvatī and the two worlds,
O radiant one, since by your greatness the Pūrus dwell between both your streams.
As such, be our protectress, O you who have the Maruts as your companions; impel the bounty of the liberal patrons.
May the auspicious Sarasvatī bring us what is auspicious; she who is never barren, the possessor of strength, takes heed.
Being praised like Jamadagni and lauded like Vasiṣṭha, may she grant us prosperity.
Desiring wives, O noble one, and desiring sons, O bounteous givers,
we invoke Sarasvat.
O Sarasvat, those waves of yours which are honeyed and dripping with clarity—
With these, be our protector.
May we enjoy the swelling breast of Sarasvatī, which is visible to all,
as well as progeny and nourishment.
At the sacrifice of heaven, at the assembly of men upon earth, where the god-seeking heroes rejoice;
where for Indra the libations are pressed, may he come for exhilaration and to the first vital strength.
We choose the divine protections; may Bṛhaspati grant us great [aid], O friends.
So that we may be sinless before the Bounteous One, who is our giver from afar like a father.
Him indeed, the eldest, the most gracious Brahmaṇaspati, I praise with reverence and oblations. May the great divine hymn attend Indra, who is the king of the prayer fashioned by the gods.
May he, Bṛhaspati, the most beloved one who possesses all boons, sit upon our sacred place;
may he grant that desire for wealth and heroic strength which we have, and carry us across our enemies unharmed.
These deathless ones, born of old, have established for us this hymn of praise, which is pleasing to the Immortal One.
We invoke Bṛhaspati, the one who cries out pure, the worshipful lord of the dwellings, the unassailable.
His powerful, ruddy horses, carrying him together, bring Bṛhaspati;
they are clothed in a ruddy form like the sky, though their dwelling place is dark blue.
For he is pure, the hundred-winged, the radiant one; he wields the golden axe, is vigorous, and wins the light.
Bṛhaspati is the sublime one who dwells within us, most skilled at providing abundant nourishment for his friends.
The two divine worlds, the parents of the god, have magnified Bṛhaspati with their greatness.
O friends, perform skillful service for the one worthy of adoration; may he provide for our prayer easy crossings and good paths.
This well-fashioned hymn has been made for you both, O Brahmaṇaspati and Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt.
Favor our prayers, awaken our inspirations, and exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who seek to harm us.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the lords of celestial wealth and of that which is on earth. Bestow riches even upon the lowly singer who praises you; protect us always with your blessings.
O Adhvaryus, offer the ruddy, milked stalk to the bull of the people.

From the cow comes the more excellent drinking-place; Indra goes day after day seeking the one who has pressed the soma. Whatever delightful food you have taken for yourself from of old, you desire its draught day by day.
Both with heart and with mind, enjoying them, O Indra, drink the offered soma-draughts, longing for them.
As soon as you were born, you drank Soma for the sake of victory; your mother proclaimed your greatness.
O Indra, you have filled the wide mid-air; through battle, you have created space for the gods.
When you fought those who considered themselves great, we overcame them as they boasted with their arms.
Or when you, O Indra, are surrounded by men and go forth to battle, may we win that glorious contest through you.
I shall proclaim the first deeds of Indra, and those new ones which the Bountiful One has performed.
When he overcame the godless illusions, then Soma became his alone.
This entire world of cattle belongs to you on every side—whatever you behold with the eye of Sūrya. O Indra, you alone are the lord of the cows; may we enjoy the wealth that you bestow.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two together rule over divine and earthly wealth.
Bestow wealth upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer; protect us always with your blessings.
Increasing beyond all measure, your body grows; they do not attain the full extent of your greatness.
We know both your regions of the earth, O Viṣṇu; as a god, you alone know the highest.
O Viṣṇu, neither one being born nor one already born has reached the further limit of your greatness, O God. You propped up the lofty, vast sky and established the eastern ridge of the earth.
For you two have become rich in nourishment, rich in milch-cows, and rich in good pasture, bestowing gifts upon man.
O Viṣṇu, you propped apart these two worlds; you have supported the earth on all sides with your rays. You two have made wide space for the sacrifice, bringing forth the sun, the dawn, and the fire.
O heroes, you struck down even the magical powers of the Dāsa Vṛṣaśipra in the contests for booty.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you two shattered the ninety-nine strong fortresses of Śambara.
Together, you struck down a hundred and a thousand of the Asura Varcin’s heroes without resistance.
This lofty hymn of praise magnifies the two great ones, the wide-striding and powerful.
O Viṣṇu, let our hymn of praise reach you at the assemblies; O Indra, cause the nourishments to swell for us in the settlements.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* call to you from my mouth; O Śipiviṣṭa, graciously accept this my oblation.
May my songs of fair praise increase your strength. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
Now the mortal who, desiring to win, offers gifts to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, shall not be harmed. He who worships with a focused mind and seeks to win such a heroic being as this—
O Viṣṇu, you who move swiftly, grant him your benevolence toward all people and your unfailing favor.
So that he may grant us abundant prosperity, wealth consisting of horses and many gladdening treasures.
Three times this god strode across this earth, which possesses a hundred hymns, by means of his greatness.
May Viṣṇu, the mightier than the mighty, be preeminent; for the name of this steadfast one is truly resplendent.
Viṣṇu strode across this earth, bestowing it upon man for his habitation. Firmly established are his praisers among the people; he, the noble-born, has created a wide dwelling-place.
Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, an Ārya, proclaim that name of yours, knowing the sacred ordinances.
I, the weak, praise you, the mighty one, who dwell in the far distance of this space.
O Viṣṇu, what was there that should have been hidden from you, when you declared, "I am Śipiviṣṭa"? Do not conceal this form from us, since you appeared in another shape in the assembly.
RV 7.100.7: O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you; O Śipiviṣṭa, graciously accept this oblation of mine.
May my well-spoken praises and songs increase your strength; and may you all protect us always with your blessings.
RV 7.101.1: Utter forth the three voices that have light as their summit, which milk from this udder the flow of honey.
Making the embryo of the plants his calf, the bull, having been born, bellows immediately.

He who is the increaser of the plants, he who is the lord of the waters, the god who rules over the whole moving world— May he grant us a triple-layered refuge, a shelter, a threefold light for our well-being.
At one time she is barren, at another she brings forth; according to his will, he has fashioned his own body.
The mother receives from her father the milk; by it the father thrives, and by it the son.
In him all worlds abide; the three heavens have flowed, and the waters have moved in three ways.
RV 7.101.4: Three reservoirs with pouring mouths drip honey all around the overflowing abundance.
RV 7.101.5: May this speech be close to Parjanya, the self-ruling lord; may he take pleasure in it from within his heart.
May there be rain-giving showers bringing us joy, and may the plants, guarded by the gods, bear good fruit.
He is the seed-bestowing bull of all things eternal; in him is the soul of all that moves and stands.
May this truth protect me for a hundred autumns; and may you always protect us with your blessings.
Sing forth to Parjanya, the bounteous son of Heaven!
May he seek out pasture for us—
Parjanya, who produces the embryo of plants, of cattle, of horses, and of women.
To him, offer this most honey-sweet oblation upon the mouth;
may he grant us continuous nourishment. Having lain still for a year, these Brahmins have observed their vows.
Stirred by Parjanya, the frogs have raised their voices;
for when the celestial waters came toward him as he lay like a parched skin in the pool,
the croaking of the frogs comes together here like the lowing of cows with their calves.
When he has rained upon these thirsty ones who longed for him as the rainy season arrived,
one goes toward the other who speaks, mocking him as a son mocks his father. One seizes the other with his hand when they have both rejoiced in the outpouring of the waters.
When the frog, rained upon, leaps about, the speckled one joins his voice with the green one.
When one of them repeats the speech of the other, like a pupil learning from a teacher,
all that they utter in the waters is like a perfectly articulated lesson.
One has the nature of a cow, one the nature of a goat; one is speckled, one of these is green.
Bearing a common name, though diverse in form, they have fashioned their speech as they speak in many ways.
Like Brahmins at the Atirātra sacrifice when the Soma is pressed, they sit around a full lake, speaking aloud.
That day of the year has arrived for you, O frogs, when the rainy season has come.
The Soma-offering Brahmins have raised their voices, performing the sacred prayer (*brahman*) that lasts throughout the year.
The Adhvaryu priests, sweating from the heated cauldrons, appear; none of them remain hidden.
The gods have guarded the ordinance of the twelfth month; these men do not violate the season.
When the rainy season has arrived at the end of the year, the heated vapors attain their release.
Gomāyu has given, Ajamāyu has given, Pṛśni has given, and Harita has given us riches.
The frogs give hundreds of cows; at the thousandfold pressing, they prolong their life.
O Indra and Soma, burn up the demons, crush them, and cast down those who thrive in darkness, O Bulls!
Drive away the thoughtless ones, scorch them, strike them dead, push them out, and pierce the devourers!
O Indra and Soma, let the evil-doer be scorched by his own sin, like a cauldron placed over fire.
Against the hater of sacred prayer, the flesh-eater with his terrible eye, against the *kimīdin*, bestow relentless hatred.
O Indra and Soma, cast the evildoers into the bottomless pit, into the darkness where there is no support.

RV_07.104.03.2 So that not even one may rise up again from this [death], let that be yours—O you who possess fury and might—for the sake of victory. RV_07.104.04.1 O Indra and Soma, hurl down from heaven your weapon, a crushing blow against the one who intends evil upon the earth.
RV_07.104.04.2 Fashion from the mountains a thunderbolt with which you may utterly consume the waxing *rakṣas*.
O Indra and Soma, turn back from heaven with those stone-hurling missiles heated by fire;
with your ageless, burning weapons, pierce the devourers in their ribs so that they go forth voiceless.
O Indra and Soma, let this prayer encompass you on every side, as a girth encompasses two spirited horses.
The oblation which I present to you both with wisdom—O lords of men, quicken these prayers as if with a sacrifice.
Remember us with your swift movements; strike down the malicious, treacherous Rākṣasas.
O Indra and Soma, let there be no easy path for the evildoer who at any time seeks to harm us with malice.

He who, with a simple mind, accuses me—who am walking my path—with false words, may he, O Indra, be like water held in a closed fist; may his speech be silenced. Those who, by their own ways, scatter him who speaks simply, or those who, by their own natures, corrupt what is auspicious—[may they be destroyed].
May Soma deliver them over to the serpent, or may he place them in the lap of Nirṛti.

O Agni, whoever seeks to harm our sap of nourishment, or our horses, or our cattle, or our bodies—may that enemy, thief, and doer of evil deeds go to destruction; may he be utterly deprived of his own body and his progeny.
May he be far away from his own body and his offspring; may he lie beneath all the three earths.
May his glory wither away, O gods, who seeks to harm us by day and by night. For the discerning person, truth and falsehood are easily distinguished; these two words have contended with one another.
Of these two, that which is true and whichever is more upright—Soma protects that; he strikes down the false.
Indeed, Soma does not further the crooked man, nor the Kṣatriya who holds [his office] falsely.
He slays the demon, he slays the one who speaks falsehood; both lie caught in the snare of Indra.
If I have been one whose gods are false, or if I have vainly imagined even the gods, O Agni—why, O Jātavedas, are you angry with us? May those of deceitful speech fall into destruction!
Today may I die if I am a sorcerer, or if I have consumed the life-breath of a man.
Then may he be separated from his ten sons—he who says to me falsely, "O sorcerer!
May Indra slay with a mighty weapon him who calls me a sorcerer though I am no sorcerer, or the demon who says, "I am pure. May he fall as the lowest of all living beings.
She who comes forth at night like an owl, hiding her body with malice—may she fall into endless pits; may the pressing-stones strike down the demons with their clatter.
Spread out, O Maruts! Search among the people! Seize the demons and crush them to pieces!

Those who fly about at night having become birds, or those who have placed enmity toward the gods during the sacrifice—O Indra, O Maghavan, hurl down the stone from heaven; sharpened by Soma, whet it well!
From the front, from behind, from below, and from above, strike down the demons with the mountain.
These very ones fly about like dog-demons; seeking to harm, they wish to injure Indra, the one who cannot be deceived.
Śakra sharpens his weapon for the treacherous; he shall surely now hurl his thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
Indra has become the destroyer of the sorcerers, the plunderer of those who steal the oblation and seek to attack us.
Indra, like an axe toward a forest, goes forth slaying the *rakṣas* as if shattering vessels.
Slay the owl-demon, the screech-owl-demon, the dog-demon, and the cuckoo-demon; Slay the eagle-demon and the vulture-demon; O Indra, crush the *rakṣas* like a millstone.

Let not the demon, accompanied by sorcery, overwhelm us; let him drive away the pairs of *kimīdins*. May the Earth protect us from earthly distress, and may the Atmosphere protect us from celestial distress. Indra, slay the male sorcerer and also the woman who exults in her magic power.
May the neckless ones, who worship false gods, perish; let them not behold the sun as it rises.
Look back, look forth; O Indra and Soma, remain awake!
Cast your weapon at the Rākṣasas, hurl the thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
